PlayerSpaceship.name: PlayerSpaceship
PlayerSpaceship.description: A PlayerSpaceship is a player-controlled ship entity. It has all the components of a ship (weapons, drives, systems) plus player-specific components (crew controls, waypoints, custom buttons). If a function name begins with "command", the function is equivalent to the crew taking a corresponding action. Such commands can be limited by the ship's capabilities, including systems damage, lack of power, or insufficient weapons stocks.

CpuShip.name: CpuShip
CpuShip.description: A CpuShip is an AI-controlled ship entity. The AI can be assigned an order (be idle, roam freely, defend location, etc.) and a combat behavior state (attack at close or long range, be evasive). AI behaviors are defined in the AIController component and its related systems. order... functions also broadcast their orders over friendly comms. Autonomous combat AI orders use the ship's short- and long-range radar ranges to acquire targets, which can be affected by radar-blocking entities. They also rank prospective targets by their type, distance, and capabilities.

SpaceStation.name: SpaceStation
SpaceStation.description: A SpaceStation is an immobile entity that repairs, resupplies, and recharges ships that dock with it. It sets several properties upon creation: - Its default callsign begins with "DS". - It restocks scan probes and CPU ship weapons by default. - It uses the scripts/comms_station.lua comms script by default. - When destroyed by damage, it awards or deducts a number of reputation points relative to its total shield strength and segments. - Any non-hostile ship can dock with it by default.

WarpJammer.name: WarpJammer
WarpJammer.description: A WarpJammer restricts the ability of any ships to use warp or jump drives within its radius. WarpJammers can be targeted, damaged, and destroyed.

Artifact.name: Artifact
Artifact.description: An Artifact is a configurable entity that can interact with other entities via collisions or scripting. Use this to define arbitrary objects or collectible pickups in scenario scripts.

Asteroid.name: Asteroid
Asteroid.description: An Asteroid is an inert piece of space terrain. Upon colliding with another entity, it deals damage and is destroyed. It has a default rotation speed, random z-offset, and model. AI-controlled entities attempt to avoid hitting them. To create a customizable collidable object, use an Artifact or SupplyDrop. For a purely decorative asteroid positioned outside of the movement plane, use a VisualAsteroid.

VisualAsteroid.name: VisualAsteroid
VisualAsteroid.description: A VisualAsteroid is a cosmetic asteroid rendered above or below the movement plane. Unlike Asteroid, it has no collision, physics, or radar trace, and does not interact with other entities. Use VisualAsteroids to add depth to asteroid fields without affecting gameplay.

Mine.name: Mine
Mine.description: A Mine is an explosive weapon that detonates and deals kinetic damage when an entity collides with its trigger range. Mines can be owned by factions but entities of any faction can trigger them. Mines can be launched from a ship's weapon tube or added by a GM or scenario script. When launched from a ship, the mine has an eject timeout, during which its trigger range is inactive. In 3D views, mines are represented by a particle effect at the center of its trigger range. To create objects with more complex collision mechanics, use an Artifact.

Nebula.name: Nebula
Nebula.description: A Nebula is a piece of space terrain with a 5U radius that blocks long-range radar, but not short-range radar. This hides any entities inside of a Nebula, as well as entities on the other side of its radar "shadow", from any ship outside of it. Likewise, a ship fully inside of a nebula has effectively no long-range radar functionality. In 3D space, a Nebula resembles a dense cloud of colorful gases.

BlackHole.name: BlackHole
BlackHole.description: A BlackHole is a piece of space terrain that pulls all nearby entities within a 5U radius, including otherwise immobile entities like stations, toward its center. An entity capable of taking damage is dealt an increasing amount of damage as it approaches the BlackHole's center. Upon reaching the center, any entity is instantly destroyed even if it's otherwise incapable of taking damage. AI behaviors avoid BlackHoles by a 2U margin. In 3D space, a BlackHole resembles a black sphere with blue horizon.

WormHole.name: WormHole
WormHole.description: A WormHole is a piece of space terrain that pulls all nearby entities within a 2.5U radius, including otherwise immobile entities like stations, toward its center. Any entity that reaches its center is teleported to another point in space. AI behaviors avoid WormHoles by a 0.5U margin.

Planet.name: Planet
Planet.description: A Planet is a spherical piece of space terrain that can orbit other entities. Each Planet has separate textures for its surface, atmosphere, and cloud layers. Several planetary textures are included in the resources/planets/ directory. Planets can collide with objects and run callback functions upon collisions.

ScanProbe.name: ScanProbe
ScanProbe.description: A ScanProbe deploys a short-range radar with a limited lifetime at a high speed to a specific point. ScanProbes can be targeted and destroyed by hostiles. It's typically launched by the relay officer and can be linked to the science radar, but can also be created by scripts. Player ships have a limited stock of ScanProbes typically replenished automatically when docked to a station or ship with the ScanProbe restocking feature enabled.

SupplyDrop.name: SupplyDrop
SupplyDrop.description: A SupplyDrop is a collectible item picked up on collision with a friendly ship. On pickup, the SupplyDrop can restock the colliding ship's weapons. Define SupplyDrop stocks and capacity with setWeaponStorage(), which doesn't have any defined maximum. If the ship has the Reactor component, the collected SupplyDrop can also recharge the ship's energy. Define SupplyDrop energy storage with setEnergy(), which doesn't have any defined maximum. A SupplyDrop can also trigger a scripting function upon pickup. Define SupplyDrop callback with onPickUp(). For a more generic entity type with similar collision properties, see Artifact.

Zone.name: Zone
Zone.description: A Zone is a polygonal area of space defined by a series of coordinates. Although a Zone is an entity, it isn't affected by physics and isn't rendered in 3D. Zones are drawn on GM, comms, and long-range radar screens, can have a text label, and can return whether an entity is within their bounds. New Zones can't be created via the exec.lua HTTP API.

methods.name: setName
methods.doc: A ModelData object contains 3D appearance and SeriousProton physics collision details. Almost all entities have a ModelData associated with them to define how they appear in 3D views. A ScienceDatabase entry can also have ModelData associated with and displayed in it. This defines a 3D mesh file, typically in OBJ format; an albedo map, or base color textures; a specular map, for shininess under lighting; an illumination map, which renders as if always lit; and a normal map, which simulates surface details. These files might be located in the resources/ directory or loaded from resource packs. ModelData also defines the model's position offset and scale relative to its mesh coordinates. If the model is for an entity with weapon components or maneuvering thrusters, ModelData also defines the origin positions of its weapon effects, and particle emitters for thruster and engine effects. For physics, ModelData defines the model's radius for a circle collider, or optional box collider dimensions. (ModelData defines 3D models, but EmptyEpsilon uses a 2D physics engine for collisions.) EmptyEpsilon loads ModelData from scripts/model_data.lua when launched, and loads meshes and textures when an entity using this ModelData is first viewed. For complete examples, see scripts/model_data.lua. Sets this ModelData's name. Use this name when referencing a ModelData from other objects.

methods.name: setMesh
methods.doc: Sets this ModelData's mesh file. Required; if omitted, this ModelData generates an error. Valid values include OBJ-format (.obj extension) 3D models relative to the resources/ directory. You can also reference models from resource packs, which have ".model" extensions. To view resource pack paths, extract strings from the pack, such as by running "strings packs/Angryfly.pack | grep -i model" on *nix. For example, this lists "battleship_destroyer_2_upgraded/battleship_destroyer_2_upgraded.model", which is a valid mesh path.
methods.example: model:setMesh("space_station_1/space_station_1.model") -- loads this model from a resource pack model:setMesh("mesh/sphere.obj") -- loads this model from the resources/ directory

methods.name: setTexture
methods.doc: Sets this ModelData's albedo map, or base flat-light color texture. Required; if omitted, this ModelData generates an error. Valid values include PNG- or JPG-format images relative to the resources/ directory. You can also reference textures from resource packs. To view resource pack paths, extract strings from the pack, such as by running "strings packs/Angryfly.pack | egrep -i (png|jpg)" on *nix.
methods.example: model:setTexture("space_station_1/space_station_1_color.jpg") -- loads this texture from a resource pack model:setTexture("mesh/ship/Ender Battlecruiser.png") -- loads this texture from the resources/ directory

methods.name: setSpecular
methods.doc: Sets this ModelData's specular map, or shininess texture. Some models use this to load a normal map. Optional; if omitted, no specular map is applied. Valid values include PNG- or JPG-format images relative to the resources/ directory. You can also reference textures from resource packs. To view resource pack paths, extract strings from the pack, such as by running "strings packs/Angryfly.pack | egrep -i (png|jpg)" on *nix.
methods.example: model:setSpecular("space_station_1/space_station_1_specular.jpg") -- loads this texture from a resource pack model:setSpecular("mesh/various/debris-blog-specular.jpg") -- loads this texture from the resources/ directory

methods.name: setIllumination
methods.doc: Sets this ModelData's illumination map, or glow texture, which defines which parts of the texture appear to be luminescent. Optional; if omitted, no illumination map is applied. Valid values include PNG- or JPG-format images relative to the resources/ directory. You can also reference textures from resource packs. To view resource pack paths, extract strings from the pack, such as by running "strings packs/Angryfly.pack | egrep -i (png|jpg)" on *nix.
methods.example: model:setIllumination("space_station_1/space_station_1_illumination.jpg") -- loads this texture from a resource pack model:setIllumination("mesh/ship/Ender Battlecruiser_illumination.png") -- loads this texture from the resources/ directory

methods.name: setNormalMap
methods.doc: Sets this ModelData's normal map. Optional; if omitted, no normal map is applied. Valid values include PNG- or JPG-format images relative to the resources/ directory, or paths defined within a resource pack loaded from the packs/ directory.
methods.example: model:setNormalMap("space_station_1/space_station_1_normal.png") -- loads this texture from a resource pack model:setNormalMap("mesh/ship/my_ship_normal.png") -- loads this texture from the resources/ directory

methods.name: setRenderOffset
methods.doc: Sets this ModelData's mesh offset, relative to its position in its mesh data. If a 3D mesh's central origin point is not at 0,0,0, use this to compensate. If you view the model in Blender, these values are equivalent to -X,+Y,+Z.
methods.example: Example: model:setRenderOffset(1,2,5) -- offsets its in-game position from its mesh file position when rendered

methods.name: setScale
methods.doc: Scales this ModelData's mesh by the given factor. Values greater than 1.0 scale the model up, and values between 0 and 1.0 scale it down. Use this if models you load are smaller or larger than expected. Defaults to 1.0.
methods.example: Example: model:setScale(20) -- scales the model up by 20x

methods.name: setRadius
methods.doc: Sets this ModelData's base radius. By default, EmptyEpsilon uses this to create a circular collider around objects that use this ModelData. setRadius() can override this for colliders. Setting a box collider with ModelData:setCollisionBox() also overrides this. Defaults to 1.0.
methods.example: Example: model:setRadius(100) -- sets the object's collisionable radius to 0.1U

methods.name: setCollisionBox
methods.doc: Sets a 2D box collider for this ModelData. If both values are greater than 0.0, this overrides ModelData:setRadius() for collisions. Defaults to 0,0.
methods.example: Example: model:setCollisionBox(400, 400) -- sets the object's collision box to 0.4U by 0.4U

methods.name: addBeamPosition
methods.doc: Adds a beam weapons origin position to this ModelData. If no origin positions are defined, this defaults to the model's origin (0,0,0). If you view the model in Blender, these coordinate values are equivalent to -X,+Y,+Z.
methods.example: -- Add a beam position at the given model X/Y/Z coordinates. model:addBeamPosition(21, -28.2, -2)

methods.name: addTubePosition
methods.doc: Adds a weapons tube origin position to this ModelData. If no origin positions are defined, this defaults to the model's origin (0,0,0). If you view the model in Blender, these coordinate values are equivalent to -X,+Y,+Z. -- Add a tube position at the given model X/Y/Z coordinates. model:addTubePosition(21, -28.2, -2)

methods.name: addEngineEmitor
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use ModelData:addEngineEmitter().

methods.name: addEngineEmitter
methods.doc: Adds an impulse engine particle effect emitter to this ModelData. When a ship engages impulse engines, this defines the position, color, and size of particle trail effects for an engine on the ship's 3D model. If no origin positions are defined, this defaults to the model's origin (0,0,0). If no mesh scale is defined, this sets it to the MeshRender default (1.0). If you view the model in Blender, these coordinate values are equivalent to -X,+Y,+Z.
methods.example: -- Add an engine emitter at model X/Y/Z coordinates -28.0, 1.5, -5.0, with a RGB color of 1.0, 0.2, 0.2 and scale of 3.0. model:addEngineEmitter(-28.0, 1.5, -5.0, 1.0, 0.2, 0.2, 3.0)

methods.name: __init__
methods.doc: A ShipTemplate defines the base functionality, stats, models, and other details for entities created from it. Entities created from ShipTemplates include those made by CpuShip(), PlayerSpaceship(), and SpaceStation(). ShipTemplates appear in ship and space station creation lists, such as the ship selection screen on scenarios that allow player ship creation, or the GM console's object creation tool. They also appear as default entries in the science database. EmptyEpsilon loads scripts/shipTemplates.lua at launch, which requires files containing ShipTemplates located in scripts/shiptemplates/. New ShipTemplates can't be defined while a scenario is running. Use Lua variables to apply several ShipTemplate functions to the same template.
methods.example: -- Create a ShipTemplate for a Cruiser Frigate-class CpuShip designated Phobos T3 template = ShipTemplate():setName("Phobos T3"):setLocaleName(_("ship","Phobos T3")):setClass(_("class","Frigate"),_("subclass","Cruiser")) -- Set the Phobos T3's appearance to the ModelData named "AtlasHeavyFighterYellow" template:setModel("AtlasHeavyFighterYellow")

methods.name: setName
methods.doc: Sets this ShipTemplate's unique reference name. Use this value for referencing this ShipTemplate in scripts. If this value begins with "Player ", including the trailing space, EmptyEpsilon uses only what follows as the name. If this ShipTemplate lacks a localized name (ShipTemplate:setLocaleName()), it defaults to this reference name.

methods.name: setLocaleName
methods.doc: Sets the displayed vessel model designation for entities created from this ShipTemplate. Use with the _ function to expose the localized name to translation.
methods.example: template:setLocaleName("Phobos T3") template:setLocaleName(_("ship","Phobos T3")) -- with a translation-exposed name

methods.name: setClass
methods.doc: Sets the vessel class and subclass for entities created from this ShipTemplate. Vessel classes are used to define certain traits across similar ships, such as dockability. See also ShipTemplate:setExternalDockClasses() and ShipTemplate:setInternalDockClasses(). For consistent class usage across translations, wrap class name strings in the _ function. Defaults to the equivalent value of (_("No class"),_("No sub-class")).

methods.name: setDescription
methods.doc: Sets the description shown in the science database for entities created from this ShipTemplate. Wrap the string with the _() function to expose it for localization. For factions and other entity types, see Entity:setDescription().
methods.example: Example: template:setDescription(_([[The Phobos T3 is most any navy's workhorse frigate.]]))

methods.name: setType
methods.doc: Sets the type of entity to create from this ShipTemplate. Defaults to "ship". Valid values are "ship", "playership", and "station". Using setType("station") is equivalent to also using ShipTemplate:setRepairDocked(true) and ShipTemplate:setRadarTrace("blip.png").

methods.name: hidden
methods.doc: If declared, this function hides this ShipTemplate from creation features and the science database. Hidden templates provide backward compatibility to older scenario scripts.

methods.name: setDefaultAI
methods.doc: Sets the default combat AI state for CPU ships created from this ShipTemplate. Combat AI states determine the AI's combat tactics and responses. They're distinct from orders, which determine the ship's active objectives and are defined by order...() functions. Valid combat AI states are: - "default" directly pursues enemies at beam range while making opportunistic missile attacks - "evasion" maintains distance from enemy weapons and evades attacks - "fighter" prefers strafing maneuvers and attacks briefly at close range while passing - "missilevolley" prefers lining up missile attacks from long range
methods.example: Example: template:setDefaultAI("fighter") -- default to the "fighter" combat AI state

methods.name: setModel
methods.doc: Sets the 3D appearance, by ModelData name, of entities created from this ShipTemplate. ModelData objects define a 3D mesh, textures, adjustments, and collision box, and are loaded from scripts/model_data.lua when EmptyEpsilon is launched.

methods.name: setDockClasses
methods.doc: As ShipTemplate:setExternalDockClasses().

methods.name: setExternalDockClasses
methods.doc: Defines a list of vessel classes that can be externally docked to entities created from this ShipTemplate. External docking keeps the docked ship attached to the outside of the carrier. By default, stations allow all classes of ships to dock externally. For consistent class usage across translations, wrap class name strings in the _ function.
methods.example: Example: template:setExternalDockClasses(_("class","Frigate"),_("class","Corvette")) -- all Frigate and Corvette ships can dock to the outside of this entity

methods.name: setInternalDockClasses
methods.doc: Defines a list of ship classes that can be docked inside of entities created from this ShipTemplate. Internal docking stores the docked ship inside of this entity. For consistent class usage across translations, wrap class name strings in the _ function.
methods.example: Example: template:setInternalDockClasses(_("class","Starfighter")) -- all Starfighter ships can dock inside of this entity

methods.name: setEnergyStorage
methods.doc: Sets the amount of energy available for player ships created from this ShipTemplate. Only player ships consume energy. Setting this for other entity types has no effect. Defaults to 1000.

methods.name: setRepairCrewCount
methods.doc: Sets the default number of repair crew for player ships created from this ShipTemplate. Defaults to 3. Only player ships use repair crews. Setting this for other entity types has no effect.

methods.name: setBeam
methods.doc: As ShipTemplate:setBeamWeapon().

methods.name: setBeamWeapon
methods.doc: Defines the traits of a BeamWeapon for entities created from this ShipTemplate. - index: Each beam weapon in this ShipTemplate must have a unique index. - arc: Sets the arc of its firing capability, in degrees. - direction: Sets the default center angle of the arc, in degrees relative to the ship's forward bearing. Value can be negative. - range: Sets how far away the beam can fire. - cycle_time: Sets the base firing delay, in seconds. System effectiveness modifies the cycle time. - damage: Sets the base damage done by the beam to the target. System effectiveness modifies the damage. To add multiple beam weapons to a ship, invoke this function multiple times, assigning each weapon a unique index value. To create a turreted beam, also add ShipTemplate:setBeamWeaponTurret(), and set the beam weapon's arc to be smaller than the turret's arc.
methods.example: Example: template:setBeamWeapon(0,90,-15,1200,3,1) -- index 0, 90-degree arc centered -15 degrees from forward, extending 1.2U, firing every 3 seconds and dealing 1 damage

methods.name: setBeamWeaponTurret
methods.doc: Converts a BeamWeapon into a turret and defines its traits for ships created from this ShipTemplate. A turreted beam weapon rotates within its turret arc toward the weapons target at the given rotation rate. - index: Must match the index of an existing beam weapon. - arc: Sets the turret's maximum targeting angles, in degrees. The turret arc must be larger than the associated beam weapon's arc. - direction: Sets the default center angle of the turret arc, in degrees relative to the ship's forward bearing. Value can be negative. - rotation_rate: Sets how many degrees per tick that the associated beam weapon's direction can rotate toward the target within the turret arc. System effectiveness modifies the rotation rate. To create a turreted beam, also add ShipTemplate:setBeamWeapon(), and set the beam weapon's arc to be smaller than the turret's arc.
methods.example: -- Makes beam weapon 0 a turret with a 200-degree turret arc centered on 90 degrees from forward, rotating at 5 degrees per tick (unit?) template:setBeamWeaponTurret(0,200,90,5)

methods.name: setBeamTexture
methods.doc: Sets the BeamEffect texture, by filename, for the BeamWeapon with the given index on ships created from this ShipTemplate. See BeamEffect:setTexture().

methods.name: setBeamWeaponEnergyPerFire
methods.doc: Sets how much energy is drained each time the BeamWeapon with the given index is fired. Only player ships consume energy. Setting this for other entity types has no effect. Defaults to 3.0, as defined in src/components/beamweapon.h.
methods.example: Example: template:setBeamWeaponEnergyPerFire(0,1) -- sets beam 0 to use 1 energy per firing

methods.name: setBeamWeaponHeatPerFire
methods.doc: Sets how much "beamweapon" system heat is generated, in percentage of total system heat capacity, each time the BeamWeapon with the given index is fired. Only player ships generate and manage heat. Setting this for other entity types has no effect. Defaults to 0.02, as defined in src/components/beamweapon.h.
methods.example: Example: template:setBeamWeaponHeatPerFire(0,0.5) -- sets beam 0 to generate 0.5 (50%) system heat per firing

methods.name: setTubes
methods.doc: Sets the number of WeaponTubes for entities created from this ShipTemplate, and the default delay for loading and unloading each tube, in seconds. Weapon tubes are 0-indexed. For example, 3 tubes would be indexed 0, 1, and 2. Ships are limited to a maximum of 16 weapon tubes. The default ShipTemplate adds 0 tubes and an 8-second loading time.
methods.example: Example: template:setTubes(6,15.0) -- creates 6 weapon tubes with 15-second loading times

methods.name: setTubeLoadTime
methods.doc: Sets the delay, in seconds, for loading and unloading the WeaponTube with the given index. Defaults to 8.0.
methods.example: Example: template:setTubeLoadTime(0,12) -- sets the loading time for tube 0 to 12 seconds

methods.name: weaponTubeAllowMissle
methods.doc: Sets which weapon types the WeaponTube with the given index can load. Note the spelling of "missle".
methods.example: Example: template:weaponTubeAllowMissle(0,"Homing") -- allows Homing missiles to be loaded in tube 0

methods.name: weaponTubeDisallowMissle
methods.doc: Sets which weapon types the WeaponTube with the given index can't load. Note the spelling of "missle".
methods.example: Example: template:weaponTubeDisallowMissle(0,"Homing") -- prevents Homing missiles from being loaded in tube 0

methods.name: setWeaponTubeExclusiveFor
methods.doc: Sets a WeaponTube with the given index to allow loading only the given weapon type.
methods.example: Example: template:setWeaponTubeExclusiveFor(0,"Homing") -- allows only Homing missiles to be loaded in tube 0

methods.name: setTubeDirection
methods.doc: Sets the angle, relative to the entity's forward bearing, toward which the WeaponTube with the given index points. Defaults to 0. Accepts negative and positive values.
methods.example: -- Sets tube 0 to point 90 degrees right of forward, and tube 1 to point 90 degrees left of forward template:setTubeDirection(0,90):setTubeDirection(1,-90)

methods.name: setTubeSize
methods.doc: Sets the weapon size launched from the WeaponTube with the given index. Defaults to "medium".
methods.example: Example: template:setTubeSize(0,"large") -- sets tube 0 to fire large weapons

methods.name: setHull
methods.doc: Sets the number of default hull points for entities created from this ShipTemplate.

methods.name: setShields
methods.doc: Sets the maximum points per shield segment for entities created from this ShipTemplate. Each argument segments the shield clockwise by dividing the arc equally for each segment, up to a maximum of 8 segments. The center of the first segment's arc always faces forward. An entity with one shield segment has only a front shield generator system, and one with two or more segments has only front and rear generator systems. If not defined, the entity defaults to having no shield capabilities.
methods.example: template:setShields(400) -- one shield segment; hits from all angles damage the same shield template:setShields(100,80) -- two shield segments; the front 180-degree shield has 100 points, the rear 80 template:setShields(100,50,40,30) -- four shield segments; the front 90-degree shield has 100, right 50, rear 40, and left 30

methods.name: setSpeed
methods.doc: Sets the impulse speed, rotational speed, and impulse acceleration for ships created from this ShipTemplate. (unit?) The optional fourth and fifth arguments set the reverse speed and reverse acceleration. If the reverse speed and acceleration aren't explicitly set, the defaults are equal to the forward speed and acceleration. See also setImpulseMaxSpeed(), setRotationMaxSpeed(), setAcceleration(). Defaults to the equivalent value of (500,10,20).
methods.example: -- Sets the forward impulse speed to 80, rotational speed to 15, forward acceleration to 25, reverse speed to 20, and reverse acceleration to the same as the forward acceleration template:setSpeed(80,15,25,20)

methods.name: setCombatManeuver
methods.doc: Sets the combat maneuver capacity for ships created from this ShipTemplate. The boost value sets the forward maneuver capacity, and the strafe value sets the lateral maneuver capacity. Defaults to (0,0).

methods.name: setWarpSpeed
methods.doc: Sets the warp speed factor for ships created from this ShipTemplate. Defaults to 0. The typical warp speed value for a warp-capable ship is 1000, which is equivalent to 60U/minute at warp 1. Setting any value also enables the "warp" system and controls.

methods.name: setSharesEnergyWithDocked
methods.doc: Defines whether entities created from this ShipTemplate supply energy to docked player ships. Defaults to true.

methods.name: setRepairDocked
methods.doc: Defines whether entities created from this template repair docked ships. Defaults to false. ShipTemplate:setType("station") sets this to true.

methods.name: setRestocksScanProbes
methods.doc: Defines whether entities created from this ShipTemplate restock scan probes on docked player ships. Defaults to false.

methods.name: setRestocksMissilesDocked
methods.doc: Defines whether entities created from this ShipTemplate restock missiles on docked CPU ships. To restock docked player ships' weapons, use a comms script. See setCommsScript() and setCommsFunction(). Defaults to false.

methods.name: setJumpDrive
methods.doc: Defines whether ships created from this ShipTemplate have a jump drive. Defaults to false.

methods.name: setJumpDriveRange
methods.doc: Sets the minimum and maximum jump distances for ships created from this ShipTemplate. Defaults to (5000,50000).
methods.example: Example: template:setJumpDriveRange(2500,25000) -- sets the minimum jump distance to 2.5U and maximum to 25U

methods.name: setCloaking
methods.doc: Not implemented. Defaults to false.

methods.name: setWeaponStorage
methods.doc: Sets the storage capacity of the given weapon type for entities created from this ShipTemplate.
methods.example: Example: template:setWeaponStorage("HVLI", 6):setWeaponStorage("Homing",4) -- sets HVLI capacity to 6 and Homing capacity to 4

methods.name: addRoom
methods.doc: Adds an empty room to a ShipTemplate. Rooms are displayed on the engineering and damcon screens. If a system room isn't accessible via other rooms connected by doors, repair crews on player ships might not be able to repair that system. Rooms are placed on a 0-indexed integer x/y grid, with the given values representing the room's upper-left corner, and are sized by damage crew capacity (minimum 1x1). To place multiple rooms, declare addRoom() multiple times.
methods.example: Example: template:addRoom(0,0,3,2) -- adds a 3x2 room with its upper-left coordinate at position 0,0

methods.name: addRoomSystem
methods.doc: Adds a room containing a ship system to a ShipTemplate. Rooms are displayed on the engineering and damcon screens. If a system room doesn't exist or isn't accessible via other rooms connected by doors, repair crews on player ships won't be able to repair that system. Rooms are placed on a 0-indexed integer x/y grid, with the given values representing the room's upper-left corner, and are sized by damage crew capacity (minimum 1x1). To place multiple rooms, declare addRoomSystem() multiple times.
methods.example: Example: template:addRoomSystem(1,2,3,4,"reactor") -- adds a 3x4 room with its upper-left coordinate at position 1,2 that contains the Reactor system

methods.name: addDoor
methods.doc: Adds a door between rooms in a ShipTemplate. Doors connect rooms as displayed on the engineering and damcon screens. All doors are 1 damage crew wide. If a system room isn't accessible via other rooms connected by doors, repair crews on player ships might not be able to repair that system. The horizontal value defines whether the door is oriented horizontally (true) or vertically (false). Doors are placed on a 0-indexed integer x/y grid, with the given values representing the door's left-most point (horizontal) or top-most point (vertical) point. To place multiple doors, declare addDoor() multiple times.
methods.example: Example: template:addDoor(2,1,true) -- places a horizontal door with its left-most point at 2,1

methods.name: setRadarTrace
methods.doc: Sets the default radar trace image for entities created from this ShipTemplate. Valid values are filenames of PNG images relative to the resources/radar/ directory. Radar trace images should be white with a transparent background. Defaults to ship.png. ShipTemplate:setType("station") sets this to blip.png.

methods.name: setLongRangeRadarRange
methods.doc: Sets the long-range radar range of ships created from this ShipTemplate. Player ships use this range on the science and operations screens' radar. AI orders of CPU ships use this range to detect potential targets. Defaults to 30000.0 (30U).
methods.example: Example: template:setLongRangeRadarRange(20000) -- sets the long-range radar range to 20U

methods.name: setShortRangeRadarRange
methods.doc: Sets the short-range radar range of ships created from this ShipTemplate. Player ships use this range on the helms, weapons, and single pilot screens' radar. AI orders of CPU ships use this range to decide when to disengage pursuit of fleeing targets. This also defines the shared radar radius on the relay screen for friendly ships and stations, and how far into nebulae that this ship can detect objects. Defaults to 5000.0 (5U).
methods.example: Example: template:setShortRangeRadarRange(4000) -- sets the short-range radar range to 4U

methods.name: setImpulseSoundFile
methods.doc: Sets the sound file used for the impulse drive sounds on ships created from this ShipTemplate. Valid values are filenames to WAV files relative to the resources directory. Use a looping sound file that tolerates being pitched up and down as the ship's impulse speed changes. Defaults to sfx/engine.wav.

methods.name: setCanScan
methods.doc: Defines whether scanning features appear on related crew screens in player ships created from this ShipTemplate. Defaults to true.

methods.name: setCanHack
methods.doc: Defines whether hacking features appear on related crew screens in player ships created from this ShipTemplate. Defaults to true.

methods.name: setCanDock
methods.doc: Defines whether the entity can dock with other entities. If true, adds an empty DockingPort component to the entity if it lacks one. If false, removes any existing DockingPort component, if any. To specify the entity's ship class for docking logic with DockingBays, use setClass() instead.

methods.name: setCanCombatManeuver
methods.doc: Defines whether combat maneuver controls appear on related crew screens in player ships created from this ShipTemplate. Defaults to true.

methods.name: setCanSelfDestruct
methods.doc: Defines whether self-destruct controls appear on related crew screens in player ships created from this ShipTemplate. Defaults to true.

methods.name: setCanLaunchProbe
methods.doc: Defines whether ScanProbe-launching controls appear on related crew screens in player ships created from this ShipTemplate. Defaults to true.

methods.name: copy
methods.doc: Returns an exact copy of this ShipTemplate and sets the new copy's reference name to the given name, as ShipTemplate:setName(). The copy retains all other traits of the copied ShipTemplate. Use this function to create variations of an existing ShipTemplate.
methods.example: -- Create two ShipTemplates: one with 50 hull points and one 50-point shield segment, -- and a second with 50 hull points and two 25-point shield segments. template = ShipTemplate():setName("Stalker Q7"):setHull(50):setShields(50) variation = template:copy("Stalker Q5"):setShields(25,25)

methods.name: setPosition
methods.doc: -- Entity base functions ----- Sets this entity's position on the map, in game units from the origin.

methods.name: getPosition
methods.doc: Returns this entity's position on the map, as X/Y coordinates in game units from the origin.

methods.name: setRotation
methods.doc: Sets this entity's absolute rotation, in degrees. Unlike setHeading(), a value of 0 points to the right of the map ("east"). The value can also be unbounded; it can be negative, or greater than 360 degrees. setHeading() and setRotation() do not change the helm's target heading on player ships. To do that, use commandTargetRotation().

methods.name: getRotation
methods.doc: Returns this entity's absolute rotation, in degrees.

methods.name: setHeading
methods.doc: Sets this entity's heading, in degrees ranging from 0 to 360. Unlike setRotation(), a value of 0 points to the top of the map ("north"), which matches player radars. Values that are negative or greater than 360 are converted to values within that range. setHeading() and setRotation() do not change the helm's target heading on player ships. To do that, use commandTargetRotation().

methods.name: getHeading
methods.doc: Returns this entity's heading, in degrees ranging from 0 to 360.

methods.name: getVelocity
methods.doc: Returns this entity's directional velocity within 2D space as an x/y vector. The values are relative x/y coordinates from the entity's current position (a 2D velocity vector).

methods.name: getAngularVelocity
methods.doc: Returns this entity's rotational velocity within 2D space, in degrees per second.

methods.name: setFaction
methods.doc: Sets the faction to which this entity belongs, by faction name. Factions are defined by the FactionInfo class, and default factions are defined in scripts/factionInfo.lua. Requires a faction name string.

methods.name: getFaction
methods.doc: Returns the name of the faction to which this entity belongs.

methods.name: getLocaleFaction
methods.doc: Returns the localized name of the faction to which this entity belongs.

methods.name: setFactionId
methods.doc: Sets the faction to which this entity belongs, by a faction entity reference. Use with getFactionId() to copy one entity's faction to another.
methods.example: Example: entity:setFactionId(other:getFactionId()) -- sets obj's faction to match other's faction

methods.name: getFactionId
methods.doc: Returns the faction list index for the faction to which this entity belongs. Use with setFactionId() to ensure that two entities belong to the same faction.

methods.name: isEnemy
methods.doc: Returns the friend-or-foe status of the given faction relative to this entity's faction. Returns true if the given entity's faction is hostile to this entity's.

methods.name: isFriendly
methods.doc: Returns the friend-or-foe status of the given faction relative to this entity's faction. Returns true if the given entity's faction is friendly to this entity's. If an entity is neither friendly nor enemy, it is neutral.

methods.name: setCommsScript
methods.doc: Sets the communications script used when this entity is hailed. Accepts the filename of a Lua script relative to the scripts/ directory. If set to an empty string, comms with this entity are disabled. The globals comms_source (player ship) and comms_target (entity) are made available in the scenario script. Some entity types set their own default comms scripts. For entity types without defaults, or when creating custom comms scripts, use setCommsMessage() to define the message and addCommsReply() to provide player response options. See also setCommsFunction().
methods.example: entity:setCommsScript("comms_custom_script.lua") -- sets scripts/comms_custom_script.lua as this entity's comms script entity:setCommsScript("") -- disables comms with this entity

methods.name: setCommsFunction
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this entity is hailed, in lieu of any current or default comms script. For a detailed example, see scripts/scenario_53_escape.lua. TODO: Confirm this: The globals comms_source (player ship) and comms_target (entity) are made available in the scenario script. They remain as globals. As usual, such globals are not accessible in required files. Instead of using the globals, the callback can optionally take two equivalent parameters. See also setCommsScript().
methods.example: entity:setCommsFunction(function(comms_source, comms_target) ... end) Example: entity:setCommsFunction(commsStation) -- where commsStation is a function that calls setCommsMessage() at least once, and uses addCommsReply() to let players respond

methods.name: setCallSign
methods.doc: Sets this entity's callsign. EmptyEpsilon generates random callsigns for entities upon creation, and this function overrides that default.

methods.name: sendCommsMessage
methods.doc: Hails a player ship from this entity. The player ship's comms position is notified and can accept or refuse the hail. If the player ship accepts the hail, this displays the given message. Returns true when the hail is accepted. Returns false if the hail is refused, or when the target player cannot be hailed right now, for example because it's already communicating with something else. This logs a message in the target's comms log. To avoid logging, use sendCommsMessageNoLog(). Requires a target player ship and message, though the message can be an empty string.

methods.name: sendCommsMessageNoLog
methods.doc: As sendCommsMessage(), but does not log a failed hail to the target ship's comms log.

methods.name: openCommsTo
methods.doc: As sendCommsMessage(), but sends an empty string as the message. This calls the entity's comms function.

methods.name: getCallSign
methods.doc: Returns this entity's callsign.

methods.name: areEnemiesInRange
methods.doc: Returns whether any entity from a hostile faction are within a given radius of this entity, in (unit?).
methods.example: Example: entity:areEnemiesInRange(5000) -- returns true if hostiles are within 5U of this entity

methods.name: getObjectsInRange
methods.doc: Returns any entity within a specific radius, in (unit?), of this entity. Returns a list of all entities within range.
methods.example: Example: entity:getObjectsInRange(5000) -- returns all entities within 5U of this entity.

methods.name: getReputationPoints
methods.doc: Returns this entity's faction reputation points.

methods.name: setReputationPoints
methods.doc: Sets this entity's faction reputation points to the given amount.

methods.name: takeReputationPoints
methods.doc: Deducts a given number of faction reputation points from this entity. Returns true if there are enough points to deduct the specified amount, then does so. Returns false and doesn't modify the value if there aren't enough points, or if the argument's value is negative.
methods.example: -- Return false if `obj` has fewer than 1000 reputation points or the passed value is negative. Otherwise, return true and deduct the points. entity:takeReputationPoints(1000)

methods.name: addReputationPoints
methods.doc: Adds a given number of faction reputation points to this entity. Discards negative values. Returns the entity.

methods.name: getSectorName
methods.doc: Returns the name of the map sector, such as "A4", where this entity is located.

methods.name: takeDamage
methods.doc: Deals a specific amount of a specific type of damage to this entity. Requires a numeric value for the damage amount, and accepts an optional DamageInfo type. The optional DamageInfo parameter can be empty, which deals "energy" damage, or a string that indicates which type of damage to deal. Valid damage types are "energy", "kinetic", and "emp". If you specify a damage type, you can also optionally specify the location of the damage's origin, for instance to damage a specific shield segment on the target. Entities by default do not implement damage, instead leaving it to specific entity types.
methods.example: entity:takeDamage(20, "emp", 1000, 0) -- deals 20 EMP damage as if it had originated from coordinates 1000,0 entity:takeDamage(20) -- deals 20 energy damage

methods.name: setDescriptions
methods.doc: Sets this entity's description in unscanned and scanned states. The science screen displays these descriptions when targeting a scanned entity. Requires two string values, one for the descriptions when unscanned and another for when it has been scanned.
methods.example: entity:setDescriptions("A refitted Atlantis X23...", "It's a trap!")

methods.name: setDescriptionForScanState
methods.doc: Sets a description for a given EScannedState on this entity. Only ship entities are created in an unscanned state. Other entities are created as fully scanned. - "notscanned" or "not": The entity has not been scanned. - "friendorfoeidentified": The entity has been identified as hostile or friendly, but has not been scanned. - "simplescan" or "simple": The entity has been scanned once under default server settings, displaying only basic information about the entity. - "fullscan" or "full": The entity is fully scanned.

methods.name: getDescription
methods.doc: Returns this entity's description for the given EScannedState. Accepts an optional string-equivalent EScannedState, which determines which description to return. Defaults to returning the "fullscan" description.
methods.example: entity:getDescription() -- returns the "fullscan" description entity:getDescription("friendorfoeidentified") -- returns the "friendorfoeidentified" description

methods.name: setRadarSignatureInfo
methods.doc: Sets this entity's radar signature, which creates noise on the science screen's raw radar signal ring. The raw signal ring contains red (electrical), green (biological), and blue (gravitational) bands of waveform noise. Certain entity types might set their own defaults or dynamically modify their signatures using this value as a baseline. Requires numeric values ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 for the gravitational, electrical, and biological radar bands, in that order. Larger and negative values are possible, but currently have no visual effect on the bands.
methods.example: Example: entity:setRadarSignatureInfo(0.0, 0.5, 1.0) -- a radar signature of 0 gravitational, 0.5 electrical, and 1.0 biological

methods.name: getRadarSignatureGravity
methods.doc: Returns this entity's gravitational radar signature value.

methods.name: getRadarSignatureElectrical
methods.doc: Returns this entity's electrical radar signature value.

methods.name: getRadarSignatureBiological
methods.doc: Returns this entity's biological radar signature value.

methods.name: setScanningParameters
methods.doc: Sets this entity's scanning complexity (number of bars in the scanning minigame) and depth (number of scanning minigames to complete until fully scanned), respectively. Setting this also clears the entity's scanned state.

methods.name: scanningComplexity
methods.doc: Returns the scanning complexity for this entity.

methods.name: scanningChannelDepth
methods.doc: Returns the maximum scanning depth for this entity.

methods.name: setScanned
methods.doc: Defines whether all factions consider this entity as having been scanned. Only ship entities are created in an unscanned state. Other entities are created as fully scanned. If false, all factions treat this entity as unscanned. If true, all factions treat this entity as fully scanned.

methods.name: isScanned
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Returns whether this entity has been scanned. Use isScannedBy() or isScannedByFaction() instead.

methods.name: isScannedBy
methods.doc: Returns whether the given entity has successfully scanned this entity.

methods.name: setScannedByFaction
methods.doc: Defines whether a given faction considers this entity as having been scanned. Requires a faction name string value as defined by its FactionInfo, and a Boolean value.

methods.name: isScannedByFaction
methods.doc: Returns whether the given faction has successfully scanned this entity. Requires a faction name string value as defined by its FactionInfo.

methods.name: onDestroyed
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this entity is destroyed by any means.
methods.example: -- Prints to the console window or logging file when this entity is destroyed entity:onDestroyed(function() print("Object destroyed!") end)

methods.name: onScanInitiated
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when a scan is initiated against this entity. The callback receives three parameters: - target: The entity being scanned (the entity this callback is registered on) - scanner: The entity performing the scan (player ship or probe) - source: The entity that initiated the scan command (player ship, or probe if scan was initiated via radar link)
methods.example: obj:onScanInitiated(function(target, scanner, source) print(target:getCallSign() .. " is being scanned by " .. scanner:getCallSign()) if source ~= scanner then print("(Scan initiated via radar-linked probe)") end end)

methods.name: onScanCompleted
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when a scan is completed against this entity. The callback receives three parameters: - target: The entity being scanned (the entity this callback is registered on) - scanner: The entity performing the scan (player ship or probe) - source: The entity that initiated the scan command (player ship, or probe if scan was initiated via radar link)
methods.example: obj:onScanCompleted(function(target, scanner, source) print(target:getCallSign() .. " has been scanned by " .. scanner:getCallSign()) if source ~= scanner then print("(Scan completed via radar-linked probe)") end end)

methods.name: onScanCancelled
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when a scan is cancelled against this entity. The callback receives three parameters: - target: The entity being scanned (the entity this callback is registered on) - scanner: The entity performing the scan (player ship or probe) - source: The entity that initiated the scan command (player ship, or probe if scan was initiated via radar link)
methods.example: obj:onScanCancelled(function(target, scanner, source) print("Scan of " .. target:getCallSign() .. " was cancelled") end)

methods.name: setLocaleName
methods.doc: Sets this faction's name as presented in the user interface. Wrap the string in the _() function to make it available for translation.

methods.name: setGMColor
methods.doc: Sets the RGB color used for entities of this faction as seen on the GM and Spectator views. Defaults to white (255,255,255).
methods.example: Example: faction:setGMColor(255,0,0) -- sets the color to red

methods.name: setEnemy
methods.doc: Sets the given faction to appear as hostile to entities of this faction. For example, Ships of this faction can target and fire at ships of the given faction. Defaults to no hostile factions. Warning: A faction can be designated as hostile to itself, but the behavior is not well-defined.
methods.example: Example: faction:setEnemy(exuari) -- sets the Exuari to appear as hostile to this faction

methods.name: setFriendly
methods.doc: Sets the given faction to appear as friendly to entities of this faction. For example, Player ships of this faction can gain reputation with it. Defaults to no friendly factions.
methods.example: Example: faction:setFriendly(human_navy) -- sets the Human Navy to appear as friendly to this faction

methods.name: setNeutral
methods.doc: Sets the given faction to appear as neutral to entities of this faction. This removes any existing faction relationships between the two factions.
methods.example: Example: faction:setNeutral(human_navy) -- sets the Human Navy to appear as neutral to this faction

methods.name: setTemplate
methods.doc: -- Template-based entity functions ----- These functions apply to entities created from a ShipTemplate, such as those created by CpuShip(), PlayerSpaceship(), and SpaceStation(). Use setTemplate() to apply a ShipTemplate's properties to an entity. Sets this ShipTemplate that defines this entity's traits, and then applies them to this entity. ShipTemplates define the entity's class, weapons, hull and shield strength, 3D appearance, and more. See the ShipTemplate class for details, and files in scripts/shiptemplates/ for the default templates. ShipTemplate string names are case-sensitive.
methods.example: CpuShip():setTemplate("Phobos T3") PlayerSpaceship():setTemplate("Phobos M3P") SpaceStation():setTemplate("Large Station")

methods.name: setShipTemplate
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use setTemplate().

methods.name: setTypeName
methods.doc: Sets this entity's vessel classification name, such as "Starfighter" or "Cruiser". This overrides the vessel class name provided by the ShipTemplate.

methods.name: getTypeName
methods.doc: Returns this entity's vessel classification name.

methods.name: getHull
methods.doc: Returns this entity's hull points.

methods.name: getHullMax
methods.doc: Returns this entity's maximum limit of hull points.

methods.name: setHull
methods.doc: Sets this entity's hull points. If set to a value larger than the maximum, this sets the value to the limit. If set to a value less than 0, this sets the value to 0. Note that setting this value to 0 doesn't immediately destroy the entity.
methods.example: Example: stbo:setHull(100) -- sets the hull point limit to either 100, or the limit if less than 100

methods.name: setHullMax
methods.doc: Sets this entity's maximum limit of hull points. If its current hull is greater than the new limit, reduce the hull to the limit.
methods.example: Example: stbo:setHullMax(100) -- sets the hull point limit to 100

methods.name: setCanBeDestroyed
methods.doc: Defines whether this entity can be destroyed by damage. Defaults to true.
methods.example: Example: stbo:setCanBeDestroyed(false) -- prevents the entity from being destroyed by damage

methods.name: getCanBeDestroyed
methods.doc: Returns whether the entity can be destroyed by damage.

methods.name: getShieldLevel
methods.doc: Returns the shield points for this entity's shield segment with the given index. Shield segments are 0-indexed.
methods.example: Example for a ship with two shield segments: stbo:getShieldLevel(0) -- returns front shield points stbo:getShieldLevel(1) -- returns rear shield points

methods.name: getShieldCount
methods.doc: Returns this entity's number of shield segments. Each segment divides the 360-degree shield arc equally for each segment, up to a maximum of 8 segments. The segments' order starts with the front-facing segment, then proceeds clockwise.

methods.name: getShieldMax
methods.doc: Returns the maximum shield points for the entity's shield segment with the given index.
methods.example: Example: stbo:getShieldMax(0) -- returns the max shield strength for segment 0

methods.name: setShields
methods.doc: Sets this entity's shield points. Each number provided as a parameter sets the points for a corresponding shield segment. Note that the segments' order starts with the front-facing segment, then proceeds clockwise. If more parameters are provided than the ship has shield segments, the excess parameters are discarded.
methods.example: -- On a ship with 4 segments, this sets the forward shield segment to 50, right to 40, rear 30, left 20 -- On a ship with 2 segments, this sets forward 50, rear 40 stbo:setShields(50,40,30,20)

methods.name: setShieldsMax
methods.doc: Sets this entity's maximum shield points per segment, and can also create new segments. The number of parameters defines the entity's number of shield segments, to a maximum of 8 segments. The segments' order starts with the front-facing segment, then proceeds clockwise. If more parameters are provided than the entity has shield segments, the excess parameters create new segments with the current shield points set to the defined max. An entity with one shield segment has only a front shield generator system, and an entity with two or more segments has only front and rear generator systems. Increasing the maximum value to a higher value than the current points does NOT automatically increase the current points, which requires a separate call to setShields().
methods.example: -- On a ship with 4 segments, this sets the forward shield max to 50, right to 40, rear 30, left 20 -- On a ship with 2 segments, this does the same, but its current rear shield points become right shield points, and the new rear and left shield segments have 0 points stbo:setShieldsMax(50,40,30,20)

methods.name: setRadarTrace
methods.doc: Sets the radar trace image for this entity. Valid values are filenames of PNG images relative to the resources/radar directory. Radar trace images should be white with a transparent background. Unscanned entities appear on player radar as their defined radar_trace.icon by default, unless radar_trace.arrow_if_not_scanned=true, in which case the entity appears as an arrow (equivalent to an argument value of "ship.png").
methods.example: entity:setRadarTrace("arrow.png") -- sets the radar trace for this entity to resources/radar/arrow.png entity:setRadarTrace("blip.png") -- displays a dot for this entity on radar when scanned

methods.name: setImpulseSoundFile
methods.doc: Sets this entity's impulse engine sound effect. Valid values are filenames of WAV files relative to the resources/ directory. Use a looping sound file that tolerates being pitched up and down as the ship's impulse speed changes.
methods.example: Example: stbo:setImpulseSoundFile("sfx/engine_fighter.wav") -- sets the impulse sound to resources/sfx/engine_fighter.wav

methods.name: getShieldsActive
methods.doc: Returns whether this entity's shields are activated. Always returns true except for player ships, because only players can deactivate shields.
methods.example: Example: stbo:getShieldsActive() -- returns true if up, false if down

methods.name: getSharesEnergyWithDocked
methods.doc: Returns whether this entity supplies energy to docked player ships.

methods.name: setSharesEnergyWithDocked
methods.doc: Defines whether this entity supplies energy to docked player ships.

methods.name: getRepairDocked
methods.doc: Returns whether this entity repairs docked ships.

methods.name: setRepairDocked
methods.doc: Defines whether this entity repairs docked ships.

methods.name: getRestocksScanProbes
methods.doc: Returns whether the entity restocks scan probes for docked player ships.

methods.name: setRestocksScanProbes
methods.doc: Defines whether the entity restocks scan probes for docked player ships.

methods.name: getRestocksMissilesDocked
methods.doc: Returns whether this entity restocks missiles for docked CPU ships.

methods.name: setRestocksMissilesDocked
methods.doc: Defines whether this entity restocks missiles for docked CPU ships. To restock docked player ships' weapons, use a comms script. See setCommsScript() and :setCommsFunction().

methods.name: getFrontShield
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use getShieldLevel() with an index value.

methods.name: getFrontShieldMax
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use getShieldMax() with an index value.

methods.name: setFrontShield
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use setShields() with an index value.

methods.name: setFrontShieldMax
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use setShieldsMax() with the appropriate number of arguments.

methods.name: getRearShield
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use getShieldLevel() with an index value.

methods.name: getRearShieldMax
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use getShieldMax() with an index value.

methods.name: setRearShield
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use setShields() with an index value.

methods.name: setRearShieldMax
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use setShieldsMax() with the appropriate number of arguments.

methods.name: onTakingDamage
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this entity takes damage. Passes the object taking damage and the instigator entity (or nil) to the function.
methods.example: Example: stbo:onTakingDamage(function(this_stbo,instigator) print(this_stbo:getCallSign() .. " was damaged by " .. instigator:getCallSign()) end)

methods.name: onTakingShieldDamage
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this entity takes damage to its shields. Passes the object taking damage to its shields and the instigator entity (or nil) to the function.
methods.example: Example: stbo:onTakingShieldDamage(function(this_stbo,instigator) print(this_stbo:getCallSign() .. " had shields damaged by " .. instigator:getCallSign()) end)

methods.name: onDestruction
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this entity is destroyed by taking damage. Passes the object taking damage and the instigator entity that delivered the destroying damage (or nil) to the function.
methods.example: Example: stbo:onDestruction(function(this_stbo,instigator) print(this_stbo:getCallSign() .. " was destroyed by " .. instigator:getCallSign()) end)

methods.name: isFriendOrFoeIdentified
methods.doc: These functions relate to ship systems, weapons, drives, docking, and other ship-specific behaviors. They apply to entities that have the relevant components, such as those created by CpuShip() and PlayerSpaceship(). [DEPRECATED] Use isFriendOrFoeIdentifiedBy() or isFriendOrFoeIdentifiedByFaction().

methods.name: isFullyScanned
methods.doc: [DEPRECATED] Use isFullyScannedBy() or isFullyScannedByFaction().

methods.name: isFriendOrFoeIdentifiedBy
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship has been identified by the given entity as either hostile or friendly.

methods.name: isFullyScannedBy
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship has been fully scanned by the given entity. See also isScannedBy().

methods.name: isFriendOrFoeIdentifiedByFaction
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship has been identified by the given faction as either hostile or friendly.

methods.name: isFullyScannedByFaction
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship has been fully scanned by the given faction. See also isScannedByFaction().

methods.name: isDocked
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship is docked with the given entity.
methods.example: Example: ship:isDocked(base) -- returns true if `ship` is fully docked with `base`

methods.name: getDockedWith
methods.doc: Returns the entity with which this ship is docked.

methods.name: getDockingState
methods.doc: Returns the EDockingState value of this ship. 0 = Not docked 1 = Docking in progress 2 = Docked

methods.name: getWeaponStorage
methods.doc: Returns the number of the given weapon type stocked by this ship.

methods.name: getWeaponStorageMax
methods.doc: Returns this ship's capacity for the given weapon type.

methods.name: setWeaponStorage
methods.doc: Sets the number of the given weapon type stocked by this entity. If the entity has MissileTubes, this sets the weapon type and amount carried by this entity. If the entity is a SupplyDrop, this sets the weapon type and amount that entity restocks upon pickup.
methods.example: ship:setWeaponStorage("Homing", 2) -- this ship has 2 Homing missiles supply_drop:setWeaponStorage("Homing", 6) -- this SupplyDrop adds 6 Homing missiles to the entity that picks it up

methods.name: setWeaponStorageMax
methods.doc: Sets this entity's capacity for the given weapon type. If this ship has more stock of that weapon type than the new capacity, its stock is reduced. However, if this ship's capacity for a weapon type is increased, its stocks are not. Use Entity:setWeaponStorage() to update the stocks.
methods.example: Example: entity:setWeaponStorageMax("Homing", 4) -- this ship can carry 4 Homing missiles

methods.name: getShieldsFrequency
methods.doc: Returns this ship's shield frequency index. To convert the index to the value used by players, multiply it by 20, then add 400.
methods.example: frequency = ship:getShieldsFrequency() -- frequency index is 10 -- Outputs "Ship's shield frequency is 600THz" print("Ship's shield frequency is " .. (frequency * 20) + 400 .. "THz")

methods.name: setShieldsFrequency
methods.doc: Sets this ship's shield frequency index. To convert the index to the value used by players, multiply it by 20, then add 400. Valid values are 0 (400THz) to 20 (800THz). Defaults to a random value. Unlike commandSetShieldFrequency(), this instantly changes the frequency with no calibration delay.
methods.example: Example: ship:setShieldsFrequency(10) -- sets the shield frequency to 600THz

methods.name: getBeamFrequency
methods.doc: Returns this ship's beam weapon frequency. To convert the index to the value used by players, multiply it by 20, then add 400.
methods.example: frequency = ship:getBeamFrequency() -- frequency index is 10 -- Outputs "Ship's beam frequency is 600THz" print("Ship's beam frequency is " .. (frequency * 20) + 400 .. "THz")

methods.name: getMaxEnergy
methods.doc: Returns this ship's energy capacity.

methods.name: setMaxEnergy
methods.doc: Sets this ship's energy capacity. CPU ships don't consume energy. Setting this value has no effect on their behavior or functionality. For player ships, see setEnergyLevelMax().

methods.name: getEnergy
methods.doc: Returns this ship's energy level.

methods.name: hasSystem
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship has the given system.
methods.example: Example: ship:hasSystem("impulse") -- returns true if the ship has impulse drive

methods.name: getSystemHackedLevel
methods.doc: Returns the hacked level for the given system on this ship. Returns a value between 0.0 (unhacked) and 1.0 (fully hacked).

methods.name: setSystemHackedLevel
methods.doc: Sets the hacked level for the given system on this ship. Valid range is 0.0 (unhacked) to 1.0 (fully hacked).
methods.example: Example: ship:setSystemHackedLevel("impulse", 0.5) -- sets the ship's impulse drive to half hacked

methods.name: getSystemHealth
methods.doc: Returns the given system's health on this ship. System health is related to damage, and is separate from its hacked level. Returns a value between -1.0 (-100%, fully disabled) and 1.0 (100%, undamaged). Values below 0.0 indicate the system is disabled.

methods.name: setSystemHealth
methods.doc: Sets the given system's health on this ship. System health is related to damage, and is separate from its hacked level. Valid range is -1.0 (-100%, fully disabled) to 1.0 (100%, undamaged). Values below 0.0 indicate the system is disabled.
methods.example: Example: ship:setSystemHealth("impulse", 0.5) -- sets the ship's impulse drive to half damaged

methods.name: getSystemHealthMax
methods.doc: Returns the given system's maximum health on this ship. Returns a value between -1.0 (-100%, fully disabled) and 1.0 (100%, undamaged).

methods.name: setSystemHealthMax
methods.doc: Sets the given system's maximum health on this ship. Valid range is -1.0 (-100%, fully disabled) to 1.0 (100%, undamaged).
methods.example: Example: ship:setSystemHealthMax("impulse", 0.5) -- limits the ship's impulse drive health to half

methods.name: getSystemHeat
methods.doc: Returns the given system's heat level on this ship. Returns a value between 0.0 (no heat) and 1.0 (overheating).

methods.name: setSystemHeat
methods.doc: Sets the given system's heat level on this ship. CPU ships don't generate or manage heat. Setting this has no effect on them. Valid range is 0.0 (no heat) to 1.0 (overheating).
methods.example: Example: ship:setSystemHeat("impulse", 0.5) -- sets the ship's impulse drive heat to half of capacity

methods.name: getSystemHeatRate
methods.doc: Returns the given system's rate of heating or cooling, in percent (0.01 = 1%) per second?, on this ship.

methods.name: setSystemHeatRate
methods.doc: Sets the given system's rate of heating or cooling, in percent (0.01 = 1%) per second?, on this ship. CPU ships don't generate or manage heat. Setting this has no effect on them.

methods.name: getSystemPower
methods.doc: Returns the given system's power level on this ship. Returns a value between 0.0 (unpowered) and 3.0 (maximum overpower). The default is 1.0.

methods.name: setSystemPower
methods.doc: Sets the given system's power level. Valid range is 0.0 (unpowered) to 3.0 (maximum overpower). The default is 1.0.
methods.example: Example: ship:setSystemPower("impulse", 0.5) -- sets the ship's impulse drive to half power

methods.name: getSystemPowerRate
methods.doc: Returns the given system's rate of consuming power, in points per second?, in this ship.

methods.name: setSystemPowerRate
methods.doc: Sets the given system's rate of consuming power, in points per second?, in this ship. CPU ships don't consume energy. Setting this has no effect.

methods.name: getSystemPowerFactor
methods.doc: Returns the relative power drain factor for the given system.

methods.name: setSystemPowerFactor
methods.doc: Sets the relative power drain factor? for the given system in this ship. "reactor" has a negative value because it generates power rather than draining it. CPU ships don't consume energy. Setting this has no effect.

methods.name: getSystemCoolant
methods.doc: Returns the coolant distribution for the given system in this ship. Returns a value between 0.0 (none) and 1.0 (capacity).

methods.name: setSystemCoolant
methods.doc: Sets the coolant quantity for the given system in this ship. CPU ships don't generate or manage heat. Setting this has no effect on them. Valid range is 0.0 (none) to 1.0 (capacity).

methods.name: getSystemCoolantRate
methods.doc: Returns the rate at which the given system in this ship takes coolant, in points per second?

methods.name: setSystemCoolantRate
methods.doc: Sets the rate at which the given system in this ship takes coolant, in points per second? CPU ships don't generate or manage heat. Setting this has no effect on them.

methods.name: getImpulseMaxSpeed
methods.doc: Returns this ship's forward and reverse impulse speed limits.
methods.example: forward,reverse = ship:getImpulseMaxSpeed() forward = ship:getImpulseMaxSpeed() -- forward speed only

methods.name: setImpulseMaxSpeed
methods.doc: Sets this ship's maximum forward and reverse impulse speeds. The reverse maximum speed value is optional. Calling this with a single argument sets both forward and reverse maximum speeds to the same value.
methods.example: ship:setImpulseMaxSpeed(30,20) -- sets the max forward speed to 30 and reverse to 20 ship:setImpulseMaxSpeed(30) -- sets the max forward and reverse speed to 30

methods.name: getRotationMaxSpeed
methods.doc: Returns this ship's maximum rotational speed, in degrees per second?

methods.name: setRotationMaxSpeed
methods.doc: Sets this ship's maximum rotational speed, in degrees per second?

methods.name: getAcceleration
methods.doc: Returns the ship's forward impulse acceleration value, in (unit?)

methods.name: setAcceleration
methods.doc: Sets the ship's forward and reverse impulse acceleration values, in (unit?) The reverse acceleration value is optional. Calling with a single argument sets both forward and reverse acceleration to the same value.
methods.example: ship:setAcceleration(5,3.5) -- sets the max forward acceleration to 5 and reverse to 3.5 ship:setAcceleration(5) -- sets the max forward and reverse acceleration to 5

methods.name: setCombatManeuver
methods.doc: Sets the ship's combat maneuvering capacities. The boost value sets the forward maneuver capacity, and the strafe value sets the lateral maneuver capacity.
methods.example: Example: ship:setCombatManeuver(400,250) -- sets boost capacity to 400 and lateral to 250

methods.name: hasJumpDrive
methods.doc: Returns whether the ship has a jump drive.

methods.name: setJumpDrive
methods.doc: Defines whether the ship has a jump drive. If true, this ship gains jump drive controls and a "jumpdrive" ship system.
methods.example: Example: ship:setJumpDrive(true) -- gives this ship a jump drive

methods.name: setJumpDriveRange
methods.doc: Sets the minimum and maximum jump distances for this ship. Defaults to (5000,50000) if not set by the ShipTemplate.
methods.example: Example: ship:setJumpDriveRange(2500,25000) -- sets the minimum jump distance to 2.5U and maximum to 25U

methods.name: setJumpDriveCharge
methods.doc: Sets this ship's current jump drive charge. Jumping depletes the ship's jump drive charge by a value equal to the distance jumped. For example, a 5U jump depletes the charge by 5000. A ship with a jump drive can jump only when this value is equal to or greater than the ship's maximum jump range. Any numeric value is valid, including negative values (longer to recharge) and values larger than the ship's maximum jump range (can jump again with a shorter, or no, recharge required). Jump drive charge regenerates at a rate modified by the "jumpdrive" system's effectiveness.

methods.name: getJumpDriveCharge
methods.doc: Returns this ship's current jump drive charge.

methods.name: getJumpDelay
methods.doc: Returns the time required by this ship to complete a jump once initiated. A ship can't perform certain actions, such as docking, while its jump delay is not 0. Returns a value between 0.0 (no delay, ready to jump) to 10.0. With normal "jumpdrive" system effectiveness, this delay is 10 seconds. System effectiveness can modify this delay.

methods.name: hasWarpDrive
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship has a warp drive.

methods.name: setWarpDrive
methods.doc: Defines whether this ship has a warp drive. If true, this ship gains warp drive controls and a "warp" ship system.

methods.name: setWarpSpeed
methods.doc: Sets this ship's warp speed factor. Valid values are any greater than 0. Ships don't tend to go faster than 24000 (1400U/min) due to engine limitations. Unlike ShipTemplate:setWarpSpeed(), setting this value does NOT also grant this ship a warp drive.

methods.name: getWarpSpeed
methods.doc: Returns this ship's warp speed factor. Actual warp speed can be modified by "warp" system effectiveness.

methods.name: getBeamWeaponArc
methods.doc: Returns the arc, in degrees, for the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship.
methods.example: Example: ship:getBeamWeaponArc(0); -- returns beam weapon 0's arc

methods.name: getBeamWeaponDirection
methods.doc: Returns the direction, in degrees relative to the ship's forward bearing, for the arc's center of the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship.
methods.example: Example: ship:getBeamWeaponDirection(0); -- returns beam weapon 0's direction

methods.name: getBeamWeaponRange
methods.doc: Returns the range for the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship.
methods.example: Example: ship:getBeamWeaponRange(0); -- returns beam weapon 0's range

methods.name: getBeamWeaponTurretArc
methods.doc: Returns the turret arc, in degrees, for the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship.
methods.example: Example: ship:getBeamWeaponTurretArc(0); -- returns beam weapon 0's turret arc

methods.name: getBeamWeaponTurretDirection
methods.doc: Returns the direction, in degrees relative to the ship's forward bearing, for the turret arc's center for the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship.
methods.example: Example: ship:getBeamWeaponTurretDirection(0); -- returns beam weapon 0's turret direction

methods.name: getBeamWeaponTurretRotationRate
methods.doc: Returns the turret's rotation rate, in degrees per tick, for the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship.
methods.example: Example: ship:getBeamWeaponTurretRotationRate(0) -- returns beam weapon 0's turret rotation rate

methods.name: getBeamWeaponCycleTime
methods.doc: Returns the base firing delay, in seconds, for the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship. Actual cycle time can be modified by "beamweapon" system effectiveness.
methods.example: Example: ship:getBeamWeaponCycleTime(0); -- returns beam weapon 0's cycle time

methods.name: getBeamWeaponDamage
methods.doc: Returns the base damage dealt by the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship. Actual damage can be modified by "beamweapon" system effectiveness.
methods.example: Example: ship:getBeamWeaponDamage(0); -- returns beam weapon 0's damage

methods.name: getBeamWeaponEnergyPerFire
methods.doc: Returns how much of this ship's energy is drained each time the BeamWeapon with the given index is fired. Actual drain can be modified by "beamweapon" system effectiveness.
methods.example: Example: ship:getBeamWeaponEnergyPerFire(0); -- returns beam weapon 0's energy use per firing

methods.name: getBeamWeaponHeatPerFire
methods.doc: Returns the heat generated by each firing of the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship. Actual heat generation can be modified by "beamweapon" system effectiveness.
methods.example: Example: ship:getBeamWeaponHeatPerFire(0); -- returns beam weapon 0's heat generation per firing

methods.name: setBeamWeapon
methods.doc: Defines the traits of a BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship. - index: Each beam weapon on this ship must have a unique index. - arc: Sets the arc of its firing capability, in degrees. - direction: Sets the default center angle of the arc, in degrees relative to the ship's forward bearing. Accepts 0, negative, and positive values. - range: Sets how far away the beam can fire. - cycle_time: Sets the base firing delay, in seconds. System effectiveness modifies the cycle time. - damage: Sets the base damage done by the beam to the target. System effectiveness modifies the damage. To create a turreted beam, also add setBeamWeaponTurret(), and set the beam weapon's arc to be smaller than the turret's arc.
methods.example: -- Creates a beam weapon with index 0, arc of 90 degrees, direction pointing backward, range of 1U, base cycle time of 1 second, and base damage of 1 point ship:setBeamWeapon(0,90,180,1000,1,1)

methods.name: setBeamWeaponTurret
methods.doc: Converts a BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship into a turret and defines its traits. A turreted beam weapon rotates within its turret arc toward the weapons target at the given rotation rate. - index: Must match the index of an existing beam weapon on this ship. - arc: Sets the turret's maximum targeting angles, in degrees. The turret arc must be larger than the associated beam weapon's arc. - direction: Sets the default center angle of the turret arc, in degrees relative to the ship's forward bearing. Accepts 0, negative, and positive values. - rotation_rate: Sets how many degrees per tick (unit?) that the associated beam weapon's direction can rotate toward the target within the turret arc. System effectiveness modifies the turret's rotation rate. To create a turreted beam, also add setBeamWeapon(), and set the beam weapon's arc to be smaller than the turret's arc.
methods.example: -- Makes beam weapon 0 a turret with a 200-degree turret arc centered on 90 degrees from forward, rotating at 5 degrees per tick (unit?) ship:setBeamWeaponTurret(0,200,90,5)

methods.name: setBeamWeaponTexture
methods.doc: Sets the BeamEffect texture, by filename, for the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship. See BeamEffect:setTexture().

methods.name: setBeamWeaponEnergyPerFire
methods.doc: Sets how much energy is drained each time the BeamWeapon with the given index is fired on this ship. Only player ships consume energy. Setting this for other entity types has no effect.
methods.example: Example: ship:setBeamWeaponEnergyPerFire(0,1) -- sets beam 0 to use 1 energy per firing

methods.name: setBeamWeaponHeatPerFire
methods.doc: Sets how much "beamweapon" system heat is generated, in percentage of total system heat capacity, each time the BeamWeapon with the given index is fired on this ship. Only player ships generate and manage heat. Setting this for other entity types has no effect.
methods.example: Example: ship:setBeamWeaponHeatPerFire(0,0.02) -- sets beam 0 to generate 0.02 (2%) system heat per firing

methods.name: setBeamWeaponArcColor
methods.doc: Sets the colors used to draw the radar arc for the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship. The first three-number value sets the RGB color for the arc when idle, and the second sets the color when firing.

methods.name: setBeamWeaponDamageType
methods.doc: Sets the damage type dealt by the BeamWeapon with the given index on this ship.
methods.example: Example: ship:setBeamWeaponDamageType(0,"emp") -- makes beam 0 deal EMP damage

methods.name: setWeaponTubeCount
methods.doc: Sets the number of WeaponTubes for this ship. Weapon tubes are 0-indexed. For example, 3 tubes would be indexed 0, 1, and 2.

methods.name: getWeaponTubeCount
methods.doc: Returns the number of WeaponTube on this ship.

methods.name: getWeaponTubeLoadType
methods.doc: Returns the weapon type loaded into the WeaponTube with the given index on this ship. Returns no value if no weapon is loaded, which includes the tube being in a loading or unloading state.

methods.name: weaponTubeAllowMissle
