methods.doc: Sets which weapon types the WeaponTube with the given index on this ship can load. Note the spelling of "missle".
methods.example: Example: ship:weaponTubeAllowMissle(0,"Homing") -- allows Homing missiles to be loaded in WeaponTube 0

methods.name: weaponTubeDisallowMissle
methods.doc: Sets which weapon types the WeaponTube with the given index can't load on this ship. Note the spelling of "missle".
methods.example: Example: ship:weaponTubeDisallowMissle(0,"Homing") -- prevents Homing missiles from being loaded in tube 0

methods.name: setWeaponTubeExclusiveFor
methods.doc: Sets a weapon tube with the given index on this ship to allow loading only the given weapon type.
methods.example: Example: ship:setWeaponTubeExclusiveFor(0,"Homing") -- allows only Homing missiles to be loaded in tube 0

methods.name: setWeaponTubeDirection
methods.doc: Sets the angle, relative to this ship's forward bearing, toward which the WeaponTube with the given index on this ship points. Accepts 0, negative, and positive values.
methods.example: -- Sets tube 0 to point 90 degrees right of forward, and tube 1 to point 90 degrees left of forward ship:setWeaponTubeDirection(0, 90):setWeaponTubeDirection(1, -90)

methods.name: setTubeSize
methods.doc: Sets the weapon size launched from the WeaponTube with the given index on this ship.
methods.example: Example: ship:setTubeSize(0,"large") -- sets tube 0 to fire large weapons

methods.name: getTubeSize
methods.doc: Returns the size of the weapon tube with the given index on this ship.

methods.name: getTubeLoadTime
methods.doc: Returns the delay, in seconds, for loading and unloading the WeaponTube with the given index on this ship.

methods.name: setTubeLoadTime
methods.doc: Sets the time, in seconds, required to load the weapon tube with the given index on this ship.
methods.example: Example: ship:setTubeLoadTime(0,12) -- sets the loading time for tube 0 to 12 seconds

methods.name: getDynamicRadarSignatureGravity
methods.doc: Returns the dynamic gravitational radar signature value emitted by this ship. Ship functions can dynamically modify this ship's radar signature values.

methods.name: getDynamicRadarSignatureElectrical
methods.doc: Returns the dynamic electrical radar signature value emitted by this ship. Ship functions can dynamically modify this ship's radar signature values.

methods.name: getDynamicRadarSignatureBiological
methods.doc: Returns the dynamic biological radar signature value emitted by this ship. Ship functions can dynamically modify this ship's radar signature values.

methods.name: addBroadcast
methods.doc: Broadcasts a message from this ship to the comms of all other ships matching the threshold. The threshold value can be an integer equivalent of EFactionVsFactionState: 0: Broadcast to all friendly ships 1: Broadcast to all friendly and neutral ships 2: Broadcast to all ships, including enemies Providing an invalid threshold value defaults to broadcasting only to friendly ships.

methods.name: setScanState
methods.doc: Sets the scan state of this ship for every faction.
methods.example: Example: ship:setScanState("full") -- every faction treats this ship as fully scanned

methods.name: setScanStateByFaction
methods.doc: Sets the scan state of this ship for a given faction.
methods.example: Example: ship:setScanStateByFaction("Kraylor","full") -- Kraylor faction treats this ship as fully scanned

methods.name: getName
methods.doc: Returns this ScienceDatabase entry's displayed name.

methods.name: getId
methods.doc: Returns this ScienceDatabase entry's unique entity.
methods.example: Examples: entry:getId() -- returns the entry's entity

methods.name: getParentId
methods.doc: Return this ScienceDatabase entry's parent entry's entity. Returns nil if the entry has no parent.
methods.example: Example: entry:getParentId() -- returns the parent entry's entity

methods.name: addEntry
methods.doc: Creates a ScienceDatabase entry with the given name as a child of this ScienceDatabase entry. Returns the newly created entry. Chaining addEntry() creates a child of the new child entry.
methods.example: species:addEntry("Canines") -- adds an entry named "Canines" as a child of ScienceDatabase species -- Adds an entry named "Felines" as a child of species, and an entry named "Calico" as a child of "Felines" species:addEntry("Felines"):addEntry("Calico")

methods.name: getEntryByName
methods.doc: Returns the first child ScienceDatabase entry of this ScienceDatabase entry found with the given name. Multiple entries can have the same name. Returns nil if no entry is found.
methods.example: Example: entry:getEntryByName("Canines") -- returns the "Canines" entry in sdb

methods.name: getEntries
methods.doc: Returns a 1-indexed table of all child entries in this ScienceDatabase entry, in arbitrary order. [NOT IMPLEMENTED YET] To return parentless top-level ScienceDatabase entries, use the global function getScienceDatabases().
methods.example: entry = getScienceDatabases()[1] -- returns the first parentless entry entry:getEntries() -- returns all of its child entries

methods.name: hasEntries
methods.doc: Returns true if this ScienceDatabase entry has child entries.

methods.name: addKeyValue
methods.doc: Adds a key/value pair to this ScienceDatabase entry's key/value data. The Database view's center column displays all key/value data when its entry is selected. Chaining addKeyValue() adds each key/value to the same entry. Warning: addKeyValue() can add entries with duplicate keys. To avoid this, use setKeyValue() instead.
methods.example: -- Adds "Legs","4" and "Ears","2" to the entry's key/value data. entry:addKeyValue("Legs","4"):addKeyValue("Ears","2") entry:addKeyValue("Legs","2") -- adds "Legs","2", even if "Legs","4" is already present

methods.name: setKeyValue
methods.doc: Sets the value of the first key/value pair matching the given key in this ScienceDatabase entry's key/value data. Key matching is case-sensitive. If the key already exists, this changes the first matching entry's value. If the key doesn't exist, this acts as addKeyValue().
methods.example: -- Assuming entry already has "Legs","4" as a key/value entry:setKeyValue("Legs","2") -- changes this entry's "Legs" value to "2" entry:setKeyValue("Arms","2") -- adds "Arms","2" to the entry's key/value data

methods.name: getKeyValue
methods.doc: Returns the value of the first matching key found in this ScienceDatabase entry's key/value data. Key matching is case-sensitive. Returns an empty string if the key doesn't exist.
methods.example: Example: entry:getKeyValue("Legs") -- returns the value if found or "" if not

methods.name: getKeyValues
methods.doc: Returns a table containing all key/value pairs in this ScienceDatabase entry. Warning: Duplicate keys appear only once, with the last value found.
methods.example: entry:getKeyValues() -- returns the key/value table for this entry for k,v in pairs(kv) do print(k,v) end -- Print each key/value pair for this entry to the console

methods.name: removeKey
methods.doc: Removes all key/value pairs matching the given key in this ScienceDatabase entry's key/value data. Key matching is case-sensitive. If duplicate matching keys exist, this removes all of them.
methods.example: Example: entry:removeKey("Legs") -- removes all key/value data with the key "Legs"

methods.name: setLongDescription
methods.doc: Sets this ScienceDatabase entry's longform description to the given string. The Database view's right column displays the longform description when its entry is selected.
methods.example: Example: entry:setLongDescription("This species is known for its loyalty...")

methods.name: getLongDescription
methods.doc: Returns this ScienceDatabase entry's longform description. Returns an empty string if no description is set.

methods.name: setImage
methods.doc: Sets this ScienceDatabase entry's image file to the given filename. Valid values are filenames to PNG files relative to the resources/ directory. An empty string removes any set image.
methods.example: Example: entry:setImage("retriever.png") -- sets the entry's image to the file "resources/retriever.png"

methods.name: getImage
methods.doc: Returns this ScienceDatabase entry's image filename. Returns an empty string if no image is set.

methods.name: setModelDataName
methods.doc: Sets the 3D appearance, by ModelData name, used for this ScienceDatabase entry. ModelData objects define a 3D mesh, textures, adjustments, and collision box, and are loaded from scripts/model_data.lua when EmptyEpsilon is launched.

methods.name: setName
methods.doc: Sets this faction's internal string name, used to reference this faction regardless of EmptyEpsilon's language setting. If no locale name is defined, this sets the locale name to the same value.
methods.example: Example: faction:setName("USN") Sets this ScienceDatabase entry's displayed name. Example: entry:setName("Species")

methods.name: setDescription
methods.doc: For factions, sets this faction's longform description as shown in its ScienceDatabase child entry. Wrap the string in the _() function to make it available for translation. For other entities, this works as setDescriptions, but sets the same description for both unscanned and scanned states. For ship templates, see ShipTemplate:setDescription().
methods.example: faction:setDescription(_("The United Stellar Navy, or USN...")) -- sets a translatable description for this faction Example: obj:setDescription("A refitted Atlantis X23 for more ...")

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sets this entity's radius. Default sizes vary by entity type. Asteroids default to random values between 110 and 130. Explosions default to 1.0. If the entity has an AvoidObject component, this also sets that radius to 2x the given value.
methods.example: Examples: obj:setSize(150) -- sets the entity's size to 150 explosion:setSize(1000) -- sets the explosion radius to 1U

methods.name: getSize
methods.doc: Returns this entity's radius. If the entity has a Physics component, this returns that value. If not, this returns the radius of its 3D mesh, or 100 by default.

methods.name: setEnergy
methods.doc: Sets this ship's energy level. Valid values are any greater than 0 and less than the energy capacity (getMaxEnergy()). Invalid values are ignored. CPU ships don't consume energy. Setting this value has no effect on their behavior or functionality. For player ships, see setEnergyLevel().
methods.example: Example: ship:setEnergy(1000) -- sets the ship's energy to 1000 if its capacity is 1000 or more Sets the amount of energy recharged upon pickup when a player ship collides with this SupplyDrop. Example: supply_drop:setEnergy(500)

methods.name: getTarget
methods.doc: Returns this ship's weapons target. For a CPU ship, this can differ from its orders target.
methods.example: Example: target = ship:getTarget() Returns this ScanProbe's target coordinates. Example: targetX,targetY = probe:getTarget()

methods.name: getOwner
methods.doc: Returns this ScanProbe's owner entity.

methods.name: setTarget
methods.doc: Sets this ScanProbe's target coordinates. If the probe has reached its target, setTarget() moves it again toward the new target coordinates.
methods.example: Example: probe:setTarget(1000,5000) Sets the BeamEffect's target entity. Requires a 3D x/y/z vector positional offset relative to the object's origin point. Example: beamfx:setTarget(target,0,0,0)

methods.name: setSource
methods.doc: Sets the BeamEffect's origin entity. Requires a 3D x/y/z vector positional offset relative to the object's origin point.

methods.name: setTexture
methods.doc: Sets the BeamEffect's texture. Valid values are filenames of PNG files relative to the resources/ directory. Defaults to "texture/beam_orange.png".

methods.name: setBeamFireSound
methods.doc: [NOT YET IMPLEMENTED] Intended to set the BeamEffect's sound effect. Valid values are filenames of WAV files relative to the resources/ directory. Defaults to "sfx/laser_fire.wav".

methods.name: setBeamFireSoundPower
methods.doc: [NOT YET IMPLEMENTED] Intended to set the magnitude of the BeamEffect's sound effect. Defaults to 1.0. Larger values are louder and can be heard from larger distances. This value also affects the sound effect's pitch.

methods.name: setDuration
methods.doc: Sets the BeamEffect's duration, in seconds. Defaults to 1.0.

methods.name: setRing
methods.doc: Defines whether the BeamEffect generates an impact ring on the target end. Defaults to true.

methods.name: setOnRadar
methods.doc: Defines whether to draw the ExplosionEffect on short-range radar. Defaults to false.

methods.name: setModel
methods.doc: Sets the 3D model used for this entity, by its ModelData name. ModelData is defined in scripts/model_data.lua.

methods.name: explode
methods.doc: Immediately destroys this entity with a visual ExplosionEffect.

methods.name: allowPickup
methods.doc: Defines whether this entity can be picked up via collision. The entity is destroyed upon being picked up. Defaults to false.

methods.name: onCollision
methods.doc: Defines a function to call every tick when an entity is colliding with the entity. Passes the entity and colliding entity to the called function.
methods.example: Example: entity:onCollision(function(entity, collider) print("Collision occurred") end)

methods.name: onPlayerCollision
methods.doc: Defines a function to call every tick when a player ship is colliding with the entity. Passes the entity and colliding player ship to the called function.
methods.example: Example: entity:onPlayerCollision(function(entity, player) print("Collision occurred") end)

methods.name: onPickUp
methods.doc: Defines a function to call once when a player ship collides with the entity and allowPickup is enabled. Passes the entity and colliding player ship to the called function.
methods.example: Example: entity:onPickUp(function(entity, player) print("Entity retrieved") end)

methods.name: onPickup
methods.doc: Alias of Entity:onPickUp().

methods.name: setSpin
methods.doc: Defines whether the entity rotates, and if so at what rotational velocity in degrees/second. For reference, normal asteroids spin at a rate between 0.1 and 0.8.

methods.name: setRadarTraceIcon
methods.doc: Sets the radar trace image for this entity. Optional. Defaults to "blip.png". Valid values are filenames to PNG files relative to resources/radar/.
methods.example: Example: entity:setRadarTraceIcon("arrow.png") -- displays an arrow instead of a blip for this entity

methods.name: setRadarTraceScale
methods.doc: Scales the radar trace for this entity. A value of 0 restores standard autoscaling relative to the entity's radius. Set to 1 to mimic ship traces.

methods.name: setRadarTraceColor
methods.doc: Sets the color of this entity's radar trace. Optional. Defaults to solid white (255,255,255)

methods.name: setAI
methods.doc: Sets the default combat AI state for this ship. Combat AI states determine the AI's combat tactics and responses. They're distinct from orders, which determine the ship's active objectives and are defined by order...() functions. Combat AI state can be set per ship, defined in the ShipTemplate, or left to "default". Valid combat AI states are: - "default" directly pursues enemies at beam range while making opportunistic missile attacks - "evasion" maintains distance from enemy weapons and evades attacks - "fighter" prefers strafing maneuvers and attacks briefly at close range while passing - "missilevolley" prefers lining up missile attacks from long range

methods.name: orderIdle
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to stay at its current position and do nothing. Idle ships don't target or attack nearby enemies.

methods.name: orderRoaming
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to roam and engage at will, without a specific target. A Roaming ship can acquire hostile targets within its long-range radar range, and prefers the best hostile target within 2U of its short-range radar range. If this ship has weapon tubes but lacks beam weapons and is out of weapons stock, it attempts to Retreat to a weapons restock target within long-range radar range.

methods.name: orderRetreat
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to move toward the given entity and dock, restock weapons, and repair its hull. If the entity is a dockable entity, this ship moves directly toward it and docks with it as soon as possible. If not, this ship moves toward the best weapons restocking target within relay range (double its long-range radar range). If this ship still can't find a restocking target, or it is fully repaired and re-stocked, this ship reverts to Roaming orders.
methods.example: Example: ship:orderRetreat(base) -- retreat to the entity `base`

methods.name: orderStandGround
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to stay at its current position and attack nearby hostiles. This ship will rotate to face a target and fires missiles within 4.5U if it has any, but won't move, roam, or patrol.

methods.name: orderDefendLocation
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to move to the given coordinates, patrol within a 1.5U radius, and attack any hostiles that move within 2U of its short-range radar range. If a targeted hostile moves more than 3U out of this ship's short-range radar range, this ship drops the target and resumes defending its position.
methods.example: Example: ship:orderDefendLocation(500, 1000) -- defend the space near these coordinates

methods.name: orderDefendTarget
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to maintain a 2U escort distance from the given entity and attack nearby hostiles. If a targeted hostile moves more than 3U out of this ship's short-range radar range, this ship drops the target and resumes escorting. If the entity being defended is destroyed, this ship reverts to Roaming orders.
methods.example: Example: ship:orderDefendTarget(base) -- defend the space near the entity `base`

methods.name: orderFlyFormation
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to fly toward the given entity and follow it from the given offset distance. This ship also targets anything its given entity targets. If the entity being followed is destroyed, this ship reverts to Roaming orders. Give multiple ships the same entity and different offsets to create a formation.
methods.example: Example: ship:orderFlyFormation(leader, 500, 250) -- fly 0.5U off the wing and 0.25U off the tail of the entity `leader`

methods.name: orderFlyTowards
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to move toward the given coordinates, and to attack hostiles that approach within its short-range radar range during transit. This ship uses any warp or jump drive capabilities to arrive near its destination. This ship disengages from combat and continues toward its destination if its target moves more than 3U out of its short-range radar range. Upon arrival, this ship reverts to the Defend Location orders with its destination as the target.
methods.example: Example: ship:orderFlyTowards(500, 1000) -- move to these coordinates, attacking nearby hostiles on the way

methods.name: orderFlyTowardsBlind
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to move toward the given coordinates, ignoring all hostiles on the way. Upon arrival, this ship reverts to the Idle orders.
methods.example: Example: ship:orderFlyTowardsBlind(500, 1000) -- move to these coordinates, ignoring hostiles

methods.name: orderAttack
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to attack the given entity.

methods.name: orderDock
methods.doc: Orders this AI-controlled ship to Fly Toward and dock with the given entity, if possible. If its target doesn't exist, revert to Roaming orders.

methods.name: getOrder
methods.doc: Returns this AI-controlled ship's current orders.

methods.name: getOrderTargetLocation
methods.doc: Returns the coordinates for this AI-controlled ship's orders. If the orders target an entity instead of coordinates, use getOrderTarget(). Some orders, such as Roaming, have no target. Returns the order's x,y coordinates, or 0,0 if not defined.

methods.name: getOrderTarget
methods.doc: Returns the target entity for this AI-controlled ship's orders. If the orders target coordinates instead of an object, use getOrderTargetLocation(). Some orders, such as Roaming, have no target. If an AI-controlled ship is engaging in combat while Roaming, its target is accessible through its Target component.

methods.name: setPlanetAtmosphereColor
methods.doc: Sets this Planet's atmospheric effect color.

methods.name: setPlanetAtmosphereTexture
methods.doc: Sets this Planet's atmospheric effect texture. Valid values are filenames of PNG files relative to the resources/ directory. Optional; if defined, atmosphere textures should be transparent or translucent. For stars, you can set an atmosphere texture such as planets/star-1.png with no surface texture.

methods.name: setPlanetSurfaceTexture
methods.doc: Sets this Planet's surface texture. Valid values are filenames of PNG files relative to the resources/ directory. Optional; if defined, surface textures should be opaque and use a 2:1-ratio equirectangular projection.

methods.name: setPlanetCloudTexture
methods.doc: Sets this Planet's cloud layer effect texture, which rotates independently of the planet. Valid values are filenames of PNG files relative to the resources/ directory. Optional; if defined, cloud layer textures should be transparent or translucent.

methods.name: getPlanetRadius
methods.doc: Returns this Planet's radius.

methods.name: setPlanetRadius
methods.doc: Sets this Planet's radius, which also sets: - its cloud radius to 1.05x this value - its atmosphere radius to 1.2x this value - its collision size to a function of this value and the planet's z-position Defaults to 5000 (5U).

methods.name: getCollisionSize
methods.doc: Returns this Planet's collision radius. Defaults to a function of the Planet's radius and its z-position. AI behaviors use this size to plot routes that try to avoid colliding with this Planet.

methods.name: setPlanetCloudRadius
methods.doc: Sets this Planet's cloud radius, overriding Planet:setPlanetRadius(). Defaults to 1.05x this Planet's radius. If this value isn't larger than the Planet's radius, the cloud layer won't be visible.
methods.example: Example: planet:setPlanetCloudRadius(2500) -- sets this Planet's cloud radius to 2.5U

methods.name: setDistanceFromMovementPlane
methods.doc: Sets the z-position of this Planet, the distance by which it's offset above (positive) or below (negative) the movement plane. This value also modifies the Planet's collision radius. Defaults to 0.
methods.example: Example: planet:setDistanceFromMovementPlane(-500) -- sets the planet 0.5U below the movement plane

methods.name: setAxialRotationTime
methods.doc: Sets this entity's axial rotation time, in seconds per full rotation. This uses the Spin component. Defaults to 0.

methods.name: setOrbit
methods.doc: Sets an entity around which this entity orbits, as well as its orbital period in seconds. Setting time to 0 will stop movement, while still being locked in orbit. An orbit can be cancelled by setting the target to nil.

methods.name: getWaypoint
methods.doc: Returns the coordinates of a waypoint with the given index that's been set by this player ship. Waypoints are 1-indexed.

methods.name: getWaypointID
methods.doc: Returns the numeric label for the given waypoint index. Waypoints are 1-indexed.

methods.name: getWaypointCount
methods.doc: Returns the total number of active waypoints owned by this player ship.

methods.name: getAlertLevel
methods.doc: Returns this player ship's EAlertLevel. Returns "Normal", "YELLOW ALERT", "RED ALERT", which differ from the valid values for commandSetAlertLevel().

methods.name: setShieldsActive
methods.doc: Defines whether this ship's shields are raised (true) or lowered (false).

methods.name: addToShipLog
methods.doc: Adds a message to this player ship's log. Takes a string as the message and a color applied to the logged message.
methods.example: ship:addToShipLog("Acknowledged", "yellow") -- adds "Acknowledged" in yellow to the `player` ship's log

methods.name: transferPlayersToShip
methods.doc: Moves all players connected to this ship to the same crew positions on another player ship. If the target lacks the PlayerControl component, or if the PlayerControl component's allowed_positions mask doesn't define any allowed crew positions, this function has no effect. Use this in scenarios to change the crew's ship.
methods.example: ship:transferPlayersToShip(player2) -- transfer all player crew to `player2`

methods.name: transferPlayersAtPositionToShip
methods.doc: Transfers only the crew members on a specific crew position to another player ship. If a player is in multiple positions, this matches any of their positions and moves that player to all of the same positions on the destination ship.
methods.example: ship:transferPlayersAtPositionToShip("helms", player2) -- transfer all crew on Helms to `player2`

methods.name: hasPlayerAtPosition
methods.doc: Returns whether a player occupies the given crew position on this ship.

methods.name: isCommsInactive
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship's comms are not in use. Use this to determine whether the player can accept an incoming hail or chat.

methods.name: isCommsOpening
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship is opening comms with another entity.

methods.name: isCommsBeingHailed
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship is being hailed by another entity.

methods.name: isCommsBeingHailedByGM
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship is being hailed by the GM.

methods.name: isCommsFailed
methods.doc: Returns whether comms to this ship have failed to open.

methods.name: isCommsBroken
methods.doc: Returns whether comms to this ship were broken off by the other entity.

methods.name: isCommsClosed
methods.doc: Returns whether comms between this ship and an entity were intentionally closed.

methods.name: isCommsChatOpen
methods.doc: Returns whether this ship is engaged in text chat with either the GM or another player ship.

methods.name: isCommsChatOpenToGM
methods.doc: Returns whether this player ship is engaged in text chat with the GM.

methods.name: isCommsChatOpenToPlayer
methods.doc: Returns whether this player ship is engaged in text chat with another player ship.

methods.name: isCommsScriptOpen
methods.doc: Returns whether this player ship is engaged in comms with a scripted entity.

methods.name: setEnergyLevel
methods.doc: Sets this ship's energy level. Values are limited from 0 to the energy level max. Negative or excess values are capped to the limits. Energy levels are relevant only if the ship also has a Reactor component.
methods.example: ship:setEnergyLevel(1000) -- sets the ship's energy to either 1000 or the max limit, whichever is lower

methods.name: setEnergyLevelMax
methods.doc: Sets this ship's energy capacity. Valid values are 0 or any positive number. If the new limit is lower than the ship's current energy level, this also reduces the energy level. Energy capacity is relevant only if the ship also has a Reactor component.
methods.example: ship:setEnergyLevelMax(1000) -- sets the ship's energy limit to 1000

methods.name: getEnergyLevel
methods.doc: Returns this ship's energy level. Energy levels are relevant only if the ship also has a Reactor component.

methods.name: getEnergyLevelMax
methods.doc: Returns this ship's energy capacity. Energy capacity is relevant only if the ship also has a Reactor component.

methods.name: getEnergyShieldUsePerSecond
methods.doc: Returns how much energy is consumed per second by this ship's shields while active. Energy consumption is relevant only if the ship also has a Reactor component.

methods.name: setEnergyShieldUsePerSecond
methods.doc: Sets how much energy is consumed per second by this ship's shields while active. Energy consumption is relevant only if the ship also has a Reactor component.

methods.name: getEnergyWarpPerSecond
methods.doc: Returns how much energy is consumed per second by this ship's warp drive while in use. Energy consumption is relevant only if the ship also has a Reactor component.

methods.name: setEnergyWarpPerSecond
methods.doc: Sets how much energy is consumed per second by this player ship's warp drive while in use. Energy consumption is relevant only if the ship also has a Reactor component.

methods.name: setMaxCoolant
methods.doc: Sets the maximum amount of coolant available to engineering on this player ship. Defaults to 10, which by default allows engineering to set 100% coolant on one system. Valid values are 0 or any positive number. If the new limit is less than the coolant already distributed, this automatically reduces distribution percentages. Coolant values are relevant only if the ship also has the Coolant component.
methods.example: ship:setMaxCoolant(5) -- halves the amount of available coolant

methods.name: getMaxCoolant
methods.doc: Returns the maximum amount of coolant available to engineering on this player ship. Coolant values are relevant only if the ship also has the Coolant component.

methods.name: setScanProbeCount
methods.doc: Sets the number of scan probes stocked by this ship. Values are limited from 0 to the scan probe count max. Negative or excess values are capped to the limits.
methods.example: ship:setScanProbeCount(20) -- sets the ship's scan probes to either 20 or the max limit, whichever is fewer

methods.name: getScanProbeCount
methods.doc: Returns the number of scan probes stocked by this ship.

methods.name: setMaxScanProbeCount
methods.doc: Sets this ship's capacity for scan probes. Valid values are 0 or any positive number. If the new limit is less than the current scan probe stock, this automatically reduces the stock.
methods.example: ship:setMaxScanProbeCount(30) -- sets the ship's scan probe capacity to 30

methods.name: getMaxScanProbeCount
methods.doc: Returns this ship's capacity for scan probes.

methods.name: addCustomButton
methods.doc: Adds a custom interactive button with the given reference name to the given crew position screen. By default, custom buttons and info are stacked in order of creation. If the reference name is unique, this creates a new button. If the reference name exists, this modifies the existing button. The caption sets the button's text label. When clicked, the button calls the given function.
methods.example: -- Add a custom button to Engineering that prints the player ship's coolant max to the console or logging file when clicked ship:addCustomButton("engineering", "get_coolant_max", "Get Coolant Max", function() print("Coolant: " .. ship:getMaxCoolant()) end)

methods.name: addCustomInfo
methods.doc: Adds a custom non-interactive info label with the given reference name to the given crew position screen. By default, custom buttons and info are stacked in order of creation. Use the order value to specify a priority. If the reference name is unique, this creates a new info. If the reference name exists, this modifies the existing info. The caption sets the info's text value.
methods.example: -- Displays the coolant max value on Engineering at or near the top of the custom button/info order ship:addCustomInfo("engineering", "show_coolant_max", "Coolant Max: " .. ship:getMaxCoolant(), 0)

methods.name: addCustomMessage
methods.doc: Displays a dismissable message with the given reference name on the given crew position screen. The caption sets the message's text.
methods.example: -- Displays the coolant max value on Engineering as a dismissable message ship:addCustomMessage("engineering", "message_coolant_max", "Coolant max: " .. ship:getMaxCoolant())

methods.name: addCustomMessageWithCallback
methods.doc: As addCustomMessage(), but calls the given function when dismissed.
methods.example: -- Displays the coolant max value on Engineering as a dismissable message, and prints "dismissed" to the console or logging file when dismissed ship:addCustomMessageWithCallback("engineering", "message_coolant_max", "Coolant max: " .. ship:getMaxCoolant(), function() print("Dismissed!") end)

methods.name: removeCustom
methods.doc: Removes the custom function, info, or message with the given reference name.
methods.example: ship:removeCustom("show_coolant_max") -- removes the custom item named "show_coolant_max"

methods.name: getBeamSystemTarget
methods.doc: Returns the index of the ESystem targeted by this player ship's weapons. Returns -1 for the hull.

methods.name: getBeamSystemTargetName
methods.doc: Returns the name of the ESystem targeted by this player ship's weapons. Returns "UNKNOWN" for the hull.

methods.name: commandTargetRotation
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to set a new target rotation. A value of 0 is equivalent to a heading of 90 degrees ("east"). Accepts 0, positive, or negative values. To objectively rotate the player ship as an entity, rather than commanding it to turn using its maneuverability, use setRotation().
methods.example: ship:commandTargetRotation(0) -- command the ship toward a heading of 90 degrees heading = 180; ship:commandTargetRotation(heading - 90) -- command the ship toward a heading of 180 degrees

methods.name: commandImpulse
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to request a new impulse speed. Valid values are -1.0 (-100%; full reverse) to 1.0 (100%; full forward). The ship's impulse value remains bound by its impulse acceleration rates.
methods.example: ship:commandImpulse(0.5) -- command this ship to engage forward half impulse

methods.name: commandWarp
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to request a new warp level. Valid values are any positive integer, or 0.

methods.name: commandJump
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to request a jump of the given distance. Valid values are any positive number, or 0, including values outside of the ship's minimum and maximum jump ranges. A jump of a greater distance than the ship's maximum jump range results in a negative jump drive charge.
methods.example: ship:commandJump(25000) -- initiate a 25U jump on the current heading

methods.name: commandAbortJump
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to abort a jump in progress.
methods.example: ship:commandAbortJump() -- aborts a jump if in progress

methods.name: commandSetTarget
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to set its weapons target to the given entity.

methods.name: commandLoadTube
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to load the WeaponTube with the given index with the given weapon type. This command respects tube allow/disallow limits.

methods.name: commandUnloadTube
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to unload the WeaponTube with the given index.

methods.name: commandFireTube
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to fire the WeaponTube with the given index. The tube fires in its current direction. To fire at a specific target, use commandFireTubeAtTarget().

methods.name: commandFireTubeAtTarget
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to fire the given weapons tube with the given entity as its target.
methods.example: ship:commandFireTubeAtTarget(0, enemy) -- command firing tube 0 at target `enemy`

methods.name: commandSetShields
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to raise (true) or lower (false) its shields.

methods.name: commandMainScreenSetting
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to change its Main Screen view to the given setting.
methods.example: ship:commandMainScreenSetting("tactical") -- command setting the main screen view to tactical radar

methods.name: commandMainScreenOverlay
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to change its Main Screen comms overlay to the given setting.
methods.example: ship:commandMainScreenOverlay("hidecomms") -- command setting the main screen view to hide the comms overlay

methods.name: commandScan
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to initiate a scan of the given entity. If the scanning mini-game is enabled, this opens it on the relevant crew screens. This command does NOT respect the player's ability to select the object for scanning, whether due to it being out of radar range or otherwise untargetable.

methods.name: commandSetSystemPowerRequest
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to set the power level of the given system. Valid values are 0 or greater, with 1.0 equivalent to 100 percent. Values greater than 1.0 are allowed.
methods.example: ship:commandSetSystemPowerRequest("impulse", 1.0) -- command setting the impulse drive power to 100%

methods.name: commandSetSystemCoolantRequest
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to set the coolant level of the given system. Valid values are from 0 to 10.0, with 10.0 equivalent to 100 percent. Values greater than 10.0 are allowed if the ship's coolant max is greater than 10.0, but controls on crew position screens are limited to 10.0 (100%).
methods.example: ship:commandSetSystemCoolantRequest("impulse", 10.0) -- command setting the impulse drive coolant to 100%

methods.name: commandDock
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to initiate docking with the given entity. This initiates docking only if the target is dockable and within docking range.

methods.name: commandUndock
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to undock from any entity it's docked with.

methods.name: commandAbortDock
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to abort an in-progress docking operation.

methods.name: commandOpenTextComm
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to hail the given entity. If the target object is a player ship or the GM is intercepting all comms, open text chat comms.

methods.name: commandCloseTextComm
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to close comms.

methods.name: commandAnswerCommHail
methods.doc: Commands whether this player ship answers (true) or rejects (false) an incoming hail.
methods.example: ship:commandAnswerCommHail(false) -- commands to reject an active incoming hail

methods.name: commandSendComm
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to select the reply with the given index during a comms dialogue.
methods.example: ship:commandSendComm(0) -- commands to select the first option in a comms dialogue

methods.name: commandSendCommPlayer
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to send the given message to the active text comms chat. This works whether the chat is with another player ship or the GM.
methods.example: ship:commandSendCommPlayer("I will destroy you!") -- commands to send this message in the active text chat

methods.name: commandSetAutoRepair
methods.doc: Commands whether repair crews on this player ship automatically move to rooms of damaged systems. Use this command to reduce the need for player interaction in Engineering, especially when combined with setAutoCoolant/auto_coolant_enabled. Crews set to move automatically don't respect crew collisions, allowing multiple crew to occupy a single space.

methods.name: commandSetBeamFrequency
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to set its beam frequency to the given value. Valid values are 0 to 20, which map to 400THz to 800THz at 20THz increments. (spaceship.cpp frequencyToString())

methods.name: commandSetBeamSystemTarget
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to target the given ship system with its beam weapons.

methods.name: commandSetShieldFrequency
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to calibrate its shield frequency to the given index. To convert the index to the value used by players, multiply it by 20, then add 400. Valid values are 0 (400THz) to 20 (800THz). Unlike setShieldsFrequency(), this initiates shield calibration to change the frequency, which disables shields for a period.

methods.name: commandAddWaypoint
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to add a waypoint at the given coordinates. This respects the 9-waypoint limit and won't add more waypoints if 9 already exist.

methods.name: commandRemoveWaypoint
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to remove the waypoint with the given index. This uses a 0-index, while waypoints are numbered on player screens with a 1-index.

methods.name: commandMoveWaypoint
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to move the waypoint with the given index to the given coordinates. This uses a 0-index, while waypoints are numbered on player screens with a 1-index.

methods.name: commandActivateSelfDestruct
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to activate its self-destruct sequence.

methods.name: commandCancelSelfDestruct
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to cancel its self-destruct sequence.

methods.name: commandConfirmDestructCode
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to submit the given self-destruct authorization code for the code request with the given index. Codes are 0-indexed. Index 0 corresponds to code A, 1 to B, etc.
methods.example: ship:commandConfirmDestructCode(0, 46223) -- commands submitting 46223 as self-destruct confirmation code A

methods.name: commandCombatManeuverBoost
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to set its forward combat maneuver to the given value. Valid values are any from -1.0 (full reverse) to 1.0 (full forward). The maneuver continues until the ship's combat maneuver reserves are depleted. Crew screens allow only forward combat maneuvers, and the combat maneuver controls do not reflect a boost set via this command.
methods.example: ship:commandCombatManeuverBoost(0.5) -- commands boosting forward at half combat maneuver capacity

methods.name: commandLaunchProbe
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to launch a ScanProbe to the given coordinates.
methods.example: ship:commandLaunchProbe(1000, 2000) -- commands launching a scan probe to coordinates x 1000, y 2000

methods.name: commandSetScienceLink
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to link the science screen to the given ScanProbe. This is equivalent to selecting a probe on Relay and clicking "Link to Science". Unlike "Link to Science", this function can link science to any given probe, regardless of which ship launched it or what faction it belongs to.
methods.example: ship:commandSetScienceLink(probe_object) -- link ScanProbe `probe` to this ship's science

methods.name: commandClearScienceLink
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to unlink the science screen from any ScanProbe. This is equivalent to clicking "Link to Science" on Relay when a link is already active.

methods.name: commandSetAlertLevel
methods.doc: Commands this player ship to set the given alert level. Valid values are "normal", "yellow", "red", which differ from the values returned by getAlertLevel().

methods.name: getRepairCrew
methods.doc: Returns a 1-indexed table of internal_crew entities that are assigned to this entity.

methods.name: getRepairCrewCount
methods.doc: Returns the number of repair crews on this entity.

methods.name: setRepairCrewCount
methods.doc: Sets the total number of repair crews on this entity. If the value is less than the number of repair crews, this function removes repair crews. If the value is greater, this function adds new repair crews to random rooms.

methods.name: isValidCrewPosition
methods.doc: Returns true if the given table of {x,y} coordinates is within one of this entity's internal rooms. or false otherwise. setRepairCrewPosition() uses this to validate target positions.
methods.example: entity:isValidCrewPosition({4,3}) -- returns false on default player Atlantis entity:isValidCrewPosition({3,2}) -- returns true on default player Atlantis

methods.name: getInternalRoomForSystem
methods.doc: Returns the internal room that contains a given ship system. Returns nil if the system is invalid, if the ship lacks internal rooms, or if no room is assigned to this system.

methods.name: getCoordinatesForInternalRoom
methods.doc: Returns a table containing tables of all valid {x,y} coordinates for a given internal room.

methods.name: moveRepairCrewToPosition
methods.doc: Sets the target coordinates of a repair crew within this entity's internal rooms. Returns a Boolean value indicating success. The crew_index is 1-indexed. If the crew_index is invalid, this returns false. If the x,y coordinates are outside of any room, this returns false. Otherwise, this returns true. Using this function to assign multiple crews to the same coordinates will stack them on the same square, which players should not be able to do!
methods.example: target_position = {3, 2} -- must be a table entity:moveRepairCrewToPosition(1, target_position)

methods.name: moveRepairCrewToRoom
methods.doc: Sets the target room of a repair crew within this entity's internal rooms, selected by passing a room. Returns a Boolean value indicating success. The crew_index is 1-indexed. If the crew_index is invalid, this returns false. The crew is assigned a random set of coordinates within the room. Using this function to assign multiple crews to the same room can stack them on the same square, which players should not be able to do!

methods.name: setAutoCoolant
methods.doc: Defines whether automatic coolant distribution is enabled on this entity. If true, coolant is automatically distributed proportionally to the amount of heat in that system. Use this command to reduce the need for player interaction in Engineering, especially when combined with commandSetAutoRepair/auto_repair_enabled.

methods.name: setControlCode
methods.doc: Sets a control code password required for a player to join this player ship. Control codes are case-insensitive.

methods.name: onProbeLaunch
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this player ship launches a probe. Passes the launching player ship and launched ScanProbe.
methods.example: -- Prints probe launch details to the console output or logging file ship:onProbeLaunch(function (player, probe) print("Probe " .. probe:getCallSign() .. " launched from ship " .. ship:getCallSign()) end)

methods.name: onProbeLink
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this player ship links a probe to the science screen. Passes the player ship and linked ScanProbe.
methods.example: -- Prints probe linking details to the console output or logging file ship:onProbeLink(function (player, probe) print("Probe " .. probe:getCallSign() .. " linked to Science on ship " .. ship:getCallSign()) end)

methods.name: onProbeUnlink
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this player ship unlinks a probe from the science screen. Passes the player ship and previously linked ScanProbe. This function is not called when the probe is destroyed or expires. See ScanProbe:onDestruction() and ScanProbe:onExpiration().
methods.example: -- Prints probe unlinking details to the console output or logging file ship:onProbeUnlink(function (player, probe) print("Probe " .. probe:getCallSign() .. " unlinked from Science on ship " .. ship:getCallSign()) end)

methods.name: getLongRangeRadarRange
methods.doc: Returns this ships's long-range radar range.

methods.name: getShortRangeRadarRange
methods.doc: Returns this player ship's short-range radar range.

methods.name: setLongRangeRadarRange
methods.doc: Sets this player ship's long-range radar range. Player ships use this range on the science and operations screens' radar.
methods.example: ship:setLongRangeRadarRange(30000) -- sets the ship's long-range radar range to 30U

methods.name: setShortRangeRadarRange
methods.doc: Sets this player ship's short-range radar range. Player ships use this range on the helms, weapons, and single pilot screens' radar. This also defines the shared radar radius on the relay screen for friendly ships and stations, and how far into nebulae that this ship can detect objects.
methods.example: ship:setShortRangeRadarRange(5000) -- sets the ship's short-range radar range to 5U

methods.name: setCanScan
methods.doc: Defines whether scanning features appear on related crew screens in this player ship.

methods.name: getCanScan
methods.doc: Returns whether scanning features appear on related crew screens in this player ship.

methods.name: setCanHack
methods.doc: Defines whether hacking features appear on related crew screens in this player ship.

methods.name: getCanHack
methods.doc: Returns whether hacking features appear on related crew screens in this player ship.

methods.name: setCanDock
methods.doc: Defines whether the "Request Docking" button appears on related crew screens in this player ship. This doesn't override any docking class restrictions set on a target ship.

methods.name: getCanDock
methods.doc: Returns whether the "Request Docking" button appears on related crew screens in this player ship.

methods.name: setCanCombatManeuver
methods.doc: Defines whether combat maneuver controls appear on related crew screens in this player ship.

methods.name: getCanCombatManeuver
methods.doc: Returns whether combat maneuver controls appear on related crew screens in this player ship.

methods.name: setCanLaunchProbe
methods.doc: Defines whether ScanProbe-launching controls appear on related crew screens in this player ship.

methods.name: getCanLaunchProbe
methods.doc: Returns whether ScanProbe-launching controls appear on related crew screens in this player ship.

methods.name: setCanSelfDestruct
methods.doc: Defines whether self-destruct controls appear on related crew screens in this player ship.

methods.name: getCanSelfDestruct
methods.doc: Returns whether self-destruct controls appear on related crew screens in this player ship. This returns false if this ship's self-destruct size and damage are both 0, even if you set setCanSelfDestruct(true).

methods.name: setSelfDestructDamage
methods.doc: Sets the amount of damage done to nearby entities when this player ship self-destructs. Any given value is randomized +/- 33 percent upon self-destruction.

methods.name: getSelfDestructDamage
methods.doc: Returns the amount of base damage done to nearby entities when this player ship self-destructs.

methods.name: setSelfDestructSize
methods.doc: Sets the radius of the explosion created when this player ship self-destructs. All entities within this radius are dealt damage upon self-destruction.
methods.example: ship:setSelfDestructSize(1500) -- sets a 1.5U self-destruction explosion and damage radius

methods.name: getSelfDestructSize
methods.doc: Returns the radius of the explosion created when this player ship self-destructs. All entities within this radius are dealt damage upon self-destruction.

methods.name: setSpeed
methods.doc: Sets this ScanProbe's speed. Probes move at a fixed rate of speed and ignore collisions and physics while moving. Defaults to 1000 (1U/second).

methods.name: getSpeed
methods.doc: Returns this ScanProbe's speed.

methods.name: setLifetime
methods.doc: Sets this ScanProbe's remaining lifetime, in seconds. Defaults to 600 seconds (10 minutes).
methods.example: Example: probe:setLifetime(60 * 5) -- sets the lifetime to 5 minutes

methods.name: getLifetime
methods.doc: Returns this ScanProbe's remaining lifetime.

methods.name: setOwner
methods.doc: Sets this ScanProbe's owner entity.

methods.name: onArrival
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this ScanProbe arrives to its target coordinates. Passes the probe and position as arguments to the function.
methods.example: Example: probe:onArrival(function(this_probe, coords) print("Probe arrived!") end)

methods.name: onExpiration
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this ScanProbe's lifetime expires. Passes the probe as an argument to the function.

methods.name: getRange
methods.doc: Returns this WarpJammer's jamming range, represented on radar as a circle with jammer in the middle. No warp/jump travel is possible within this radius.

methods.name: setRange
methods.doc: Sets this WarpJammer's jamming radius. No warp/jump travel is possible within this radius. Defaults to 7000.0.
methods.example: Example: jammer:setRange(10000) -- sets a 10U jamming radius

methods.name: setTargetPosition
methods.doc: Sets the target teleportation coordinates for entities that pass through the center of this wormhole. Avoid the default value of {0,0}, which should be treated as no destination.

methods.name: getTargetPosition
methods.doc: Returns the target teleportation coordinates for entities that pass through the center of this wormhole. The default value of {0,0} should be treated as no destination.

methods.name: onTeleportation
methods.doc: Defines a function to call when this WormHole teleports an entity. Passes the WormHole object and the teleported entity.
methods.example: -- Outputs teleportation details to the console window and logging file wormhole:onTeleportation(function(this_wormhole,teleported_object) print(teleported_object:getCallSign() .. " teleported to " .. this_wormhole:getTargetPosition()) end)

methods.name: setPoints
methods.doc: Sets the corners of this Zone n-gon to x_1, y_1, x_2, y_2, ... x_n, y_n. Positive x coordinates are right/"east" of the origin, and positive y coordinates are down/"south" of the origin in space. This also moves the Zone's Transform coordinates to the new centroid via setPosition().
methods.example: Example: zone:setPoints(2000,0, 0,3000, -2000,0) -- defines a triangular zone

methods.name: setColor
methods.doc: Sets this Zone's color when drawn on radar. Defaults to white (255,255,255).

methods.name: setLabel
methods.doc: Sets this Zone's text label, rendered at the zone's center point.

methods.name: getLabel
methods.doc: Returns this Zone's text label.

methods.name: setLocalSkybox
methods.doc: Sets this Zone's local skybox. Optionally also sets this zone's skybox fade transition distance, which defaults to 0.
methods.example: zone:setLocalSkybox("purple", 250) -- sets this zone's local skybox to "purple" with a 0.25U transition distance zone:setLocalSkybox("purple") -- sets the local skybox but doesn't modify the fade distance

methods.name: isInside
methods.doc: Returns whether the given entity is inside this Zone.
methods.example: Example: zone:isInside(obj) -- returns true if `obj` is within the zone's bounds

methods.name: orderRoamingAt
methods.doc: Declared in scripts/api/cpuship.lua
